Initial Inquiries.name: Investigaciones iniciales
Initial Inquiries.text:
Teniendo en cuenta el plan expuesto en el @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd]{Capítulo 3: El complot del mal}, los PJs curiosos pronto discernirán que hay algo siniestro en marcha en la Ciudad del Lobo Blanco. Después de haber llegado a Middenheim, haber lidiado con la emboscada de la Mano Púrpura y haber encontrado el malvado complot de @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} es probable que quieran saber más sobre esta secta e intentar destruirla. Además, es posible que quieran dar con @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard von Wittgenstein} y poner al descubierto la secta de Slaanesh a la que pertenece. Cuando se encuentren con los skaven (@UUID[JournalEntry.yXOEsyeWgRgbeVmc.JournalEntryPage.QBR9vcY928EotGA2]{‘El Caos ataca de Noche’}), puede que también quieran perseguirlos, tras haberse visto frustrados en su anterior encuentro en el castillo Wittgenstein. Lo último que esperan es verse inmersos en un complot para derribar la ciudad y que manipula a sus habitantes más poderosos.

Esta trama se detalla en el resto del libro. La Mano Púrpura, los skaven y el trotamundos de Gotthard von Wittgenstein están todos implicados en mayor o menor medida: seguir una u otra de estas líneas de investigación conduce a la trama principal de la aventura, y viceversa.

Es probable que estas investigaciones iniciales tengan lugar en los dos días anteriores a la semana del carnaval, cuando comiencen a orientarse por Middenheim. Como opción, pueden tener la oportunidad de encontrarse con algunos de los PNJs principales más sociables y menos solitarios, como el campeón del Graf, las damas de la corte, el montero mayor y el juglar de la corte, pero sólo si se encuentran en el lugar y el momento adecuados (ver @UUID[JournalEntry.yXOEsyeWgRgbeVmc.JournalEntryPage.jddY9IUXGz1Call1#encountering-npcs]{‘Encuentros con los PNJs’})

Para Grognards: ¡Sigan ese complot!

'‘Lo último que esperan – dice el primer párrafo de este capítulo– es verse inmersos en un complot para derribar la ciudad y que manipula a sus habitantes más poderosos’. Si los jugadores son veteranos de la campaña de la primera edición, esto será lo primero que esperen. Puede que pasen de todo lo demás y empiecen a tratar de hacer conexiones en la corte de inmediato, lo que, aunque no desbarata la aventura, le quita algo de encanto a la experiencia. Aquí hay algunas sugerencias para los DJ que se encuentren con esta situación.

Los recuadros @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.KlRr9LX8GFAD5bbk#the-villain]{'El villano'} y @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.KlRr9LX8GFAD5bbk#deadly-secrets]{'Secretos mortales'} ofrecen opciones para realizar cambios que devuelvan el desafío de esta aventura a los jugadores que ya la han terminado antes. Una vez que éstos se den cuenta de que los papeles de varios PNJs importantes se han intercambiado, estarán más dispuestos a volver al principio y comenzar una investigación desde cero. Aunque los jugadores sigan convencidos de que saben qué PNJs son los mejores para abordar, el problema sigue siendo una presentación adecuada. La sección @UUID[JournalEntry.yXOEsyeWgRgbeVmc.JournalEntryPage.jddY9IUXGz1Call1#encountering-npcs]{‘Encuentros con los PNJs’} demuestra lo valioso que puede ser cada PNJ principal en este sentido y lo fácil –o difícil– que es llegar a conocerlos.

Una vez conseguido el encuentro, los aventureros deben ser capaces de convencer a un PNJ importante de que saben qué está pasando, lo cual significa que deben ser capaces de hablar con conocimiento de causa sobre la situación, argumentando bien sus sospechas y presentando pruebas convincentes. Esto es muy difícil de hacer si los jugadores tiran de memoria o si no han conseguido un nivel de confianza y fama al ocuparse de otros asuntos.

Aunque la identidad del villano no cambie y otros detalles sigan siendo los mismos que en la primera edición, los PJs encontrarán más difícil saltarse las primeras partes de la aventura de lo que puedan suponer los jugadores grognards. La aventura deja de centrarse en cómo pueden descubrir la verdad los PJs –aunque todavía tienen que hacerlo, con independencia de lo que sus respectivos jugadores descubran– y pasa a fijarse más en cómo se las arreglan para entrar en la alta sociedad de Middenheim. Esto ofrece un desafío diferente, que es posible que los jugadores no se esperen.

Gotthard von Wittgenstein.name: Gotthard von Wittgenstein
Gotthard von Wittgenstein.text:
El apellido de von Wittgenstein no significa nada para nadie en Middenheim: el castillo y las tierras de la familia están demasiado lejos para que el nombre resulte familiar, y Gotthard adoptó el alias ‘@UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard Wallenstein}’ cuando se trasladó a la ciudad. Además, los PJs sólo tienen una vaga idea de su aspecto por un retrato que pudieron ver en el @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.musGjY0nSDY6gPY4.JournalEntryPage.9QbqTbEIM76lCVab]{castillo}. Sin embargo, esto no tiene por qué ser así. Aunque es preferible que no lo identifiquen muy rápido, la búsqueda del último Wittgenstein puede añadir profundidad e intriga a la aventura y ofrecerte algunas formas de ayudar a un grupo que está teniendo dificultades.

Hay varios actos en el carnaval donde los PJs podrían ver a Gotthard: todos están listados en su tarjeta de PNJ y a todos ellos asisten otros PNJs importantes, a los que es posible que los aventureros les interese conocer, y más a medida que avance la semana. Aunque Gotthard no guarda una particular amistad con ninguno de los demás PNJs, un grupo que los siga tendrá sin duda la oportunidad de verlo. Pese a que su rostro no les resulte familiar, cualquier PJ que se acerque a menos de 2 yardas puede hacer un Chequeo Desafiante (+0) de Percepciónpara darse cuenta de que lleva un anillo con el escudo de los Wittgenstein en el dedo meñique de la mano derecha.

Si un encuentro fortuito te parece demasiado aleatorio, los PJs podrían ver a Gotthard en un evento @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.W5W0W99G4olBLGzw#the-garden-party-(marktag,-4–8:00-p.m.)]{Fiesta del Jardín} acribillando de atenciones no deseadas a una @UUID[JournalEntry.PkTZGuhuMoy1xLWa.JournalEntryPage.ClmMNlSphPvcNVTy]{dama de la corte}. Espoleados por la galantería y el deseo de que un PNJ esté en deuda con ellos, los PJs acuden al rescate y en el proceso descubren el anillo revelador.

Otra opción es encontrar a Gotthard por estar involucrado en la @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba]{secta del Cetro de Jade}. Tras conocer la existencia de la misma a través de un miembro de la Mano Púrpura capturado (ver más atrás) o por algún otro medio, los aventureros pueden deducir a partir de la carta de Gotthard a su hermana y de la capilla de Slaanesh que había en el castillo que es probable que Gotthard sea miembro de este culto. Una investigación cuidadosa podría llevarlos a una fiesta privada: si vigilan el lugar, es posible que vean a Gotthard entrando.

Otra opción es encontrar a Gotthard por estar involucrado en la secta del Cetro de Jade. . Armados con el conocimiento de que el mercader más influyente de la ciudad pertenece a una familia maldita, que tiene un nombre falso y que es miembro de una secta del Caos que adora a Slaanesh, puede que los PJs decidan acercarse a él y hacerle chantaje. Esto lleva a la pregunta: ¿qué quieren de Gotthard, exactamente? Es posible que el grupo no lo haya pensado hasta ese momento, pero él puede decirles poco sobre la familia que no sepan ya, después de haber estado fuera durante tanto tiempo. Si se entera de que sus familiares están muertos y que el castillo ha quedado destruido, Gotthard aprovechará cualquier oportunidad para escapar. Contratará a asesinos para acabar con los PJs y permanecerá oculto hasta que está seguro de que han acabado el trabajo.

La identidad de Wallenstein

Lo ideal es que el grupo descubra la verdadera identidad de Gotthard la noche de festag, en un momento en que estén enfrascados en la trama principal de la aventura. Si lo ven por ahí, es siempre en lugares públicos concurridos, donde tienen pocas posibilidades de un acercamiento directo.

Cuando se enteren de que ‘Wallenstein’ es el presidente de un gremio influyente y de una poderosa Komission de la ciudad, se darán cuenta (con la ayuda de un Chequeo Desafiante (+0) de Sabiduría académica (derecho) o similar) de que sería muy imprudente acusar a un ciudadano prominente de algo sin una prueba abrumadora y la ayuda de otros ciudadanos importantes.

Dado que apoya los nuevos impuestos públicamente, los PJs harían bien en empezar a investigarlo ahí, sobre todo si ya saben o sospechan que la Mano Púrpura está involucrada en los impuestos (ver más atrás). Esta estrategia les permitirá reunir pruebas antes de hacer una acusación, y en el camino pueden conocer a otros poderosos PNJs y descubrir el complot para reemplazar al @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris}.

Una pizca de paranoia

Aunque el @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba]{Cetro de Jade} no comparte la afición de la Mano Púrpura por el color de sus prendas, los jugadores no tienen por qué saberlo. Ponle de vez en cuando un chaleco verde oscuro a un PNJ sospechoso. Cuantas más dudas tengan sobre en quién pueden confiar, mejor.

The Purple Hand.name: La Mano Púrpura
The Purple Hand.text:
Si los PJs sobreviven a la emboscada inicial de los sectarios de la Mano Púrpura (ver @UUID[JournalEntry.OYXb3CKZ79qBHCHK.JournalEntryPage.0eO10ZKGO0gm7Lz8]{‘Una mano púrpura de bienvenida’}), no habrá más ataques organizados: una vez que comience el carnaval, los líderes de la secta estarán enfrascados en el complot para apoderarse de Middenheim. Aun así, siempre cabe la posibilidad de que, en algún momento de la aventura, un sectario de la Mano Púrpura reconozca a ‘Lieberung’. Habrá un momento de contacto visual, una expresión de sorpresa, quizás una señal de manos, diferente a cualquiera que los PJs hayan visto antes y que signifique ‘informar a los líderes’ y luego el sectario intentará perderse entre la multitud. Tienen la opción de intentar seguir o capturar a este individuo (ver @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.occHCt6k2KgETwRX]{‘Las multitudes’}), pero no será una tarea fácil.

Si los aventureros lo consiguen, quizá descubran dónde hay un piso franco de la Mano Púrpura y capturen a uno o dos sectarios, pero serán individuos de bajo rango que sólo saben de tres o cuatro compañeros de su célula y el hecho de que se les ha ordenado cesar toda otra actividad (incluidos los esfuerzos por recuperar a ‘Lieberung’) y centrar sus esfuerzos en aumentar el apoyo popular a los nuevos impuestos.

A elección del DJ, un sectario capturado puede completar algunos detalles que los PJs pasaron por alto en aventuras anteriores: el cargo importante de Lieberung en la secta, su promesa de entregar la herencia y el significado de cualquier signo de la secta que pueda llamar la atención de los PJs. 

Sin embargo, los peones de la organización no saben que Wasmeier es uno de los suyos (uno de sus líderes, de hecho) ni ningún detalle de la trama, más allá del hecho de que los nuevos impuestos son muy importantes para la cúpula de la secta.

Los miembros de poco nivel no conocen el nombre de @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard von Wittgenstein}, Los miembros de poco nivel no conocen el nombre de Gotthard von Wittgenstein, pero quizá sepan que hay una célula de la secta de Slaanesh activa en la ciudad. Un sectario excepcionalmente bien informado puede saber incluso que esta secta se llama el Cetro de Jade y que sobre todo recluta a miembros entre los jóvenes ociosos y ricos de la ciudad. Ambas sectas son rivales, pero no enemigas, y no han emprendido ninguna acción abierta contra la otra: el Cetro de Jade sólo busca el placer, mientras que la Mano Púrpura aspira al poder, y ya tiene miembros en las altas esferas, aunque los mindundis de la secta desconozcan la identidad de éstos.

Algo muy grande

Un resultado inesperado de interrogar a un miembro de la secta capturado, podría ser la noticia de que el magister magistri, el líder supremo de la Mano Púrpura, ha ordenado suspender todas las operaciones durante la semana de carnaval, y esto incluye la captura de Kastor Lieberung.

Nadie sabe por qué (los sectarios de a pie no son quién para cuestionarse las órdenes del magister), pero ha habido rumores dentro de la secta de que se planea algo muy grande. A la célula del sectario capturado le ordenaron a que pasara desapercibida hasta nueva orden y no hacer nada, excepto seguir apoyando los nuevos impuestos todo lo posible. Nota: esta ha sido una orden general desde que los impuestos fueron propuestos por primera vez hace unas semanas.

Esta revelación puede llevar a los PJs a sospechar que la Mano Púrpura está detrás de alguna manera tras los nuevos impuestos e incluso que los impuestos tienen un papel en el misterioso ‘gran plan’ que se materializará en la semana del carnaval. Esto debería de motivarlos a que empiecen a investigar los impuestos (ver @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.LHLPCNetl8UKzaXx]{‘Los impuestos’}).

Esa posible que los jugadores emprendedores vayan más allá y decidan que cualquiera que apoye los impuestos es un sectario de la Mano Púrpura en potencia. Si van con cuidado y buscan prendas de color morado que ayuden a confirmar sus sospechas, serán capaces de atrapar a algunos sectarios más de poca monta, pero no podrán averiguar nada más.

Claro que no todos los que defienden a capa y espada los nuevos impuestos son miembros de la secta, y es posible que los PJs imprudentes se den cuenta de que han capturado a las personas equivocadas y que van a meterse en problemas. Los middenheimers inocentes no dudarán en denunciarlos a la Guardia si escapan o los liberan; los oficinistas y escribas de la Komission de Comercio, Oficios e Impuestos harán lo mismo y la noticia de su calvario llegará también a oídos de Gotthard Wallenstein (véase más adelante), que tramará represalias; es probable que los Hijos de Ulric regresen con un gran número de amigos, musculosos y decididos, para enseñarles a los forasteros una lección que puede terminar muy mal; etc. Después de unos cuantos incidentes problemáticos, es probable que los jugadores decidan que la mejor manera de localizar a la Mano Púrpura es investigar los impuestos en sí.

La táctica de Kastor Lieberung

A estas alturas, el grupo ha tenido mucho tiempo para desarrollar una profunda enemistad con la Mano Púrpura. Si el PJ que se parece a Kastor Lieberung sigue vivo, es probable que haya sufrido debido a ello. Sin embargo, aunque este parecido fuera un lastre a lo largo de El Enemigo en las Sombras y Muerte en el Reik, la ciudad de Middenheim ofrece oportunidades para que los PJs astutos lo conviertan en una ventaja.

La organización de la Mano Púrpura (ver @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.IZVgB7zmTm4rK2yJ]{La Mano Púrpura}) es obtusa, enrevesada, está llena de maquinaciones internas y en ciertas ocasiones resulta directamente contradictoria, lo cual complace muchísimo a Tzeentch. Esto es algo que podría beneficiar al grupo. La Mano Púrpura hace un intento de capturarlos o matarlos a su llegada a Middenheim, aunque durante el carnaval la mayoría de las actividades de la secta se van a suspender, pero los PJs seguirán encontrándose con sectarios por la ciudad o cuando la Mano les envíe asesinos si se acercan demasiado a desentrañar sus planes durante la semana de festejos.

Un enfoque plausible para ‘Kastor’ sería convencer a algunos sectarios de Middenheim de que, en realidad, la recompensa que se ofrecía por Kastor Lieberung se debía a los politiqueos internos de la Mano Púrpura, tal vez a una disputa entre los líderes sectarios de Nuln y los de Middenheim. La mayoría de los miembros no están al tanto del gran plan, por lo que no se corre el riesgo de desentrañar toda la trama antes de tiempo. Un ‘Kastor’ en especial persuasivo puede convencer a algunos sectarios de baja estofa de que le presten ayuda, sobre todo si han tenido la oportunidad de aprender algunas señales de mano y términos de la secta. Algunas entrevistas prolongadas con los sectarios podrían incluso justificar que un PJ tuviera la oportunidad de aprender el Talento @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.sYbgpSnRqSZWgwFP]{Etiqueta (Mano Púrpura)} como si fuera parte de su carrera actual. 

¿Cómo podrían los jugadores sacar provecho de esto? Bueno, quizá la Mano Púrpura haya estado vigilando a sus rivales del Cetro de Jade y puede guiar al grupo hacia Gotthard Wallenstein. Aunque la Mano Púrpura no tiene ningún agente cercano al Graf que no se haya nombrado ya, es posible que cuente con algunos miembros de menor rango entre el personal del palacio. Estos se podrían utilizar para conseguir acceso a ciertas zonas restringidas, adquirir fondos o material para el chantaje o incluso para poner sobre aviso a los PJs respecto a ‘Frau Kenner’ (ver @UUID[JournalEntry.XUBjQIBMN6QpERPY.JournalEntryPage.DEJD9QuE8LLH9xfT]{El traidor desenmascarado}) que suministra @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.jTFOrokjEHbi12rT]{Delicia de Ranald} al Canciller. Incluso pueden proporcionar algo de fuerza bruta en ciertas ocasiones, aunque la secta cuenta con tales métodos que ello debería incomodar a muchos PJs. 

Es importante, claro está, que ninguno de estos agentes conozca la identidad real de Wasmeier: deberías poner gran cuidado en no relacionar la secta con él de ninguna manera. Si ello pasara, asegúrate de reafirmar la desagradable realidad de que los PJs cuentan con sectarios entre sus aliados. Deberían escuchar relatos de los terribles actos llevados a cabo en el pasado en nombre de Tzeentch y la esperanza de que pasarán cosas similares en el futuro y, por supuesto, que la Mano también espera que Kastor esté allí.

El no va más de la moda

Mientras los PJs recorren todos los estratos de la sociedad de Middenheim, seguro que estarán atentos a la moda que ha elegido la Mano Púrpura: llevar una prenda de vestir de color morado. Esto asegura que todos los sectarios se reconozcan entre sí en público. Por supuesto, no todo el mundo que se pone una gorra púrpura, lleva un monedero índigo o luce un fajín morado es un sectario, así que esta es una excelente oportunidad para sembrar la paranoia entre los jugadores. Cada vez que necesites describir la apariencia de un PNJ, utiliza la tabla de abajo para generar una prenda púrpura al azar si deseas crear un poco de inquietud.

@Table[purple-hand-clothing]

The Taxes.name: The Taxes
The Taxes.text:
@UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.LHLPCNetl8UKzaXx]{The Taxes}

Sooner or later, the Characters should come to the conclusion that it would be worthwhile to find out more about the new tax laws that have upset so many people. Depending on their careers, personalities, and inclinations, they have several possible sources, each of which can provide certain information. Of course, each of these sources has its own point of view, which complicates matters somewhat: some ambiguities or downright contradictions may arise, requiring the Characters to sift through the snippets of information they have amassed and put the pieces together as best they can. The GM should not be afraid to repeat items: observant Players realise that confirmations are valuable.

General Sentiments

Reactions to the new taxes vary widely. Apart from a few, described above — who think the taxes are an Ulrican plot to force out other religions, an Altdorfer conspiracy to weaken the city in preparation for conquest and subjugation, a profiteering move by the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild}, or an Elven plot against the city’s Dwarfs — the majority of Middenheimers do not much care one way or the other. So long as they are unaffected, the taxes are someone else’s problem. A few may grumble about delays at the gates, but that is all.

If the Characters are especially slow to realise the deeper implications of the taxes, they may overhear some bar-room pundit holding forth on the contributions of the Dwarfs, the wizards, and the priests to Middenheim’s construction and defence. Over the jeers and groans of his listeners, this prophet of doom loudly maintains that someone high up in the government is trying to drive them all out, clearly for some sinister purpose. Most people, though, are concerned with the pleasures of the Carnival, and with their own day-to-day worries.

Those directly affected by the taxes have a different attitude. Any Dwarf is furious about the Dwarf Tax, both at the cost, and at the insult it represents to the Dwarven race: ‘No Elf Tax, is there? Halfling Tax? Not on your life? Human Tax? Now that one would make some money — but no. It’s an outrage, so it is, and by stone and steel we won’t stand for it!’

Wizards, alchemists, and priests, while privately fuming, are less vocal until they know they are among friends. The Guild and the various temples are pursuing the matter, they are sure, and the Graf is not an unreasonable man: this is clearly some mistake, and will shortly be corrected. Of course, there are always a few individuals who react more strongly, especially after a few drinks, and students at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.PJSTe8IXwh6oy78t]{Collegium Theologica} may take the opportunity to abandon their classes for a day of protests, drinking, and general rowdiness. They may hope to arouse more widespread public indignation, but mostly they will succeed in annoying their fellow citizens.

Only a few people are enthusiastically in favour of the new taxes. Elves smirk and joke about the Dwarf Tax, and those with reason to dislike wizards or priests do the same about those taxes, but almost no one vocally supports all three measures.

The exception is members of the Purple Hand, who have been instructed by their superiors to promote the taxes at every opportunity. However, they have little idea why the taxes are important, and their arguments may seem ill-informed and unconvincing.

Eventually, this constant background noise should prompt the Characters to seek information from reliable sources. This may include various guilds, Komissions, temples, and any major NPCs whose acquaintance is the way into the main part of the adventure.

The following information can be gained from Middenheimers of all types. The tone and some minor details might be altered to reflect the nature of the informant: a drunkard can only tell a little, a barman a little more, and a modestly-educated merchant more still. Educated people, if asked specific questions they are unable to answer, and direct the Characters to an appropriate source for further information.

When Were the Taxes Passed?

The tax changes were introduced just under a month ago. Some taxes are taken when entering and leaving the city, and a widespread belief is that they have been introduced to coincide with Carnival, to rake in more money from visitors. Others are taken at the end of every month. The first monthly payment is due at the end of the Carnival. So far, the authorities have been very zealous about collecting them.

Who Sets the Tax Laws?

The average citizen can only give partial, and sometimes misleading, information. By far the most common reply points to the @UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Chancellor}, since his prime role is the implementation of fiscal policy. Other candidates are the Graf and the Law Lords, both being seen as great wielders of power. A more enlightened informant may direct the Characters to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.kWRpev3g5D6QqxYA]{Worshipful GuiId of Legalists}, saying that they can get a fuller version there.

Graf Boris and his Advisors

It is common knowledge that @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} is ailing and depends heavily on his advisors. Some — the @UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Chancellor}, the Law Lords, the ‘@UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Princess}’ — are widely known as influential, while some are not; no one knows, for example, that the Graf has a paramour. Some major NPCs are more socially visible than others: the Chancellor, being a recluse, is hardly known by most people, while the @UUID[Actor.nzNgV71abEH1iNFo]{Court Minstrel}, a real extrovert, is better-known.

The Graf ’s Sons

The common folk are dimly aware that @UUID[Actor.dfVVZJ41NVDpWkNy]{Stefan} has some kind of health issue, but know little of him and have never seen him. @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Heinrich} is a more interesting case. He is not particularly well-known among the general public, for he adopts a low profile in social life, and is out of the city for long periods of time. However, most Middenheimers should be able to give at least a vague description of him, ‘HUGE man, he is — a giant!’.

Red Herrings

Some folk give credence to bizarre rumours. Graf Boris is controlled by Daemons; he converses with a magical oracular pool in the palace; or any of a dozen equally wild tales. 

In general, the people holding these views also believe that the world is flat, that Mannslieb is made of cheese, and so on, and the Characters should have cause to doubt them. Of course, certain rumours are more widespread: for example, Rallane is frequently blamed for the Dwarf Tax (although not for the others), and the Midden Marshals are generally thought to have more political influence than they do.

The City Councils

There are three councils that are relevant to this stage of the adventure: the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.kWRpev3g5D6QqxYA]{Worshipful Guild of Legalists}, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.rCpAPw22cl9dsEnl]{Komission for Commerce, Trade, and Taxation}, and the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.h1NmGWYdOpGvgrbg]{Komission for Elven, Dwarven and Halfling Interests}. Their offices are open from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm. Asking questions at any of the other City Councils is  a waste of time.

They generally work on the same principle: an enquirer explains the nature of the enquiry to a clerk, who then wanders off to locate the person best able to deal with the question. This can take anything up to an hour, but a 15-minute wait is average. Of course, if the enquirer has subsequent questions, or if the original question was phrased ambiguously, then another official may have to be found.

For the questions the Characters may ask, the correct official is named; on future visits they can ask for him or her personally and save time, cutting the average waiting time to 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.kWRpev3g5D6QqxYA]{The Worshipful Guild Of Legalists}

This guild has many functions connected with the law. Indeed, it was they who drafted the new taxes, but it is not their job to formulate original policy. They deal in facts in vast quantities — and prepare official versions for release to the public.

Clerk Hubergreiber, a low-ranking clerk, is the man to see about the tax laws. He is able to provide a summary of the @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.LHLPCNetl8UKzaXx]{information}: who is taxed, when, how often, and how much. He can say, if asked, that the tax was implemented less than one month ago, and that the first monthly collection is due the day after the Carnival ends. The Guild is looking for more scribes to handle the monumental quantity of paperwork required by the new laws. Hubergreiber may offer a job to any character with the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.GogGbYxkVdCmiKqf]{Read/Write} Talent, especially if they also have Art (Writing) or Art (Calligraphy).

Who Sets the Tax Laws?

Senior Clerk Wahnsinnige can discuss this in a very dry, bureaucratic manner. The GM should read the players the following information more or less verbatim:

The interests of merchants, and similar people are represented by the Chairman of the Merchants’ Guild, who makes recommendations to the City Komission for Commerce, Trade, and Taxation. The current Chairman of the Guild — Herr Gotthard Wallenstein — is also, as it happens, Chairman of the Komission.

Other interested bodies, such as the temples and the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.PJSTe8IXwh6oy78t]{Collegium Theologica}, make their representations via other city Councils, according to the nature of the matter at hand: in some cases the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.2QMwt6sDAfJ6Rjt1]{Komission for Health, Education and Welfare}; in others the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.QpoN5fivtBT60AY1]{Komission for Public Works}; and so on.

The @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.rCpAPw22cl9dsEnl]{Komission for Commerce, Trade, and Taxation} then makes representations to the Law Lords. The Law Lords weigh up the matter, and the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.kWRpev3g5D6QqxYA]{Worshipful Guild of Legalists} assists in the drafting of proposed legislation. The resulting document is put before the @UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Chancellor}, who may make further recommendations, and then before the Graf. The Graf then weighs up the matter after discussing it with other advisors, and may pass the legislation, return it with directions for amendment, or, in rare cases, reject it.

The @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.kWRpev3g5D6QqxYA]{Worshipful Guild of Legalists} does not itself have any role in forming policy, but merely drafts the laws as directed by the Law Lords, after due and aforementioned consultation.

As to the advisors to whom the Graf may turn for comments on proposed legislation, Graf Boris may consult anyone who he feels is qualified to render useful advice.

This tells the Characters very little, and a tiresome encounter it is too, although the gist is simple enough: the Graf speaks to anyone he wants, listens to anyone he wants, and everyone else does what he wants.

The Law Lords

Any questions about the role of the Law Lords is referred to Clerk Valberik, who is able to summarise the workings of the Law Lords: they vote on policy in secret meetings, and the majority decision is put to the Graf. If the decision is not unanimous, differences of opinion are never revealed.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.h1NmGWYdOpGvgrbg]{The Komission For Elven, Dwarven, and Halfling Interests}

The Council was set up over a hundred years ago when there was tension between Elves and Dwarfs, and both communities felt ill-treated by the Human majority in the city. The ruler at the time thought it a wise move to institute this official channel to care for their interests, and did not want to offend the more placid Halflings by leaving them out. It is now not very active, but is responsible for organising some of the nonhuman cultural events in the Carnival. Waiting and bureaucracy here are minimal.

General Enquiries

A nonhuman character can arrange for an interview here on almost any pretext. Enquiries are usually dealt with by a staff member of the same race as the enquirer: Dwarfs are met by Clerk Thognar, Elves by Clerk Malondel, and Halflings by Clerk Huggins. Both Elf and Halfling have little to say, except that the Dwarf Tax sets a bad precedent. In addition, Malondel points out that with many Elves following wizardry as a profession, the Scroll Tax is causing concern. Humans can see Thognar about the Dwarf Tax, or Malondel about the Scroll Tax, if they express concern and seem interested in doing something about it.

Rallane and the Dwarf Tax

If Malondel is asked about the court minstrel @UUID[Actor.nzNgV71abEH1iNFo]{Rallane Lafarel}, and his possible role in the Dwarf Tax, he looks most disapproving and say that this is a scurrilous rumour spread about by people who ought to know better. The view held by Elves (and Halflings) is that it is simply a money-grabbing exercise by the @UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Chancellor}.

If Clerk Thognar is asked about this, he tries to hides his seething anger. He explains that the Dwarfs are collecting a petition complaining at great length to Graf Boris, ‘and we can count on your signatures, of course?’ If he is taken out after work for a drink, he becomes more forthcoming (unless there are any Elves with the party) and denounce Rallane as the person responsible for the tax: ‘He hates our people, and other folk think we’re all rich because we work hard — that’s probably how he got support for the idea.’

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.rCpAPw22cl9dsEnl]{The Komission For Commerce, Trade, and Taxation}

Although this is an obvious place to enquire about the tax changes, the Chairman of the Council, @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard Wallenstein}, is almost never here, and neither he nor the senior clerk Franz Christoph Becker agrees to see the Characters anyway. Clerk Udiller sees the Characters but, following his masters’ lead, will say little. Given half a chance, the clerk directs the Characters to another council or guild, saying that the Komission’s job is simply to collect the taxes in the most efficient way: ‘It’s nothing to do with us, really.’ This Komission is gaining a reputation for doing nothing for anyone but the merchants.

The Guilds

These institutions exist to promote the interests of their members. Middenheim, like any other large city, has its fair share of guilds, though for this adventure only four are relevant: the Grand Guild of Wizards, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild}, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.CX77jCGRkysWfOKy]{Dwarven Engineers’ Guild}, and — though not exactly a guild — the loose-knit community of Middenheim’s underworld.

On visiting a guild, an individual is asked to provide a membership number. If he or she is not a member, provisional acceptance can be made for the duration of Carnival week. This costs a gold crown, and the character must prove eligibility for membership by answering some profession-related questions. A guild does not deal with persons who are not members.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.m0gDOo9sztuTymsb]{The Grand Guild Of Wizards}

At this stage, no one — not even a wizard — can get a meeting with the @UUID[Actor.sN0PeIFSOidPua1f]{High Wizard} or his @UUID[Actor.ZVVaOEUN9ArYrYnM]{Deputy}, but the Characters can try to by-pass formal procedure and try to meet them in a public or social encounter.

Even so, the guildhouse is bustling with Wizards and Apprentices: some looking for news; some looking for contacts with Wizards in other cities besides Altdorf; and some simply looking for like-minded folk to vent their frustrations. Feelings are running high: some wizards have already left Middenheim to avoid the monthly tax, though the majority are waiting to see if an eleventh-hour agreement can be reached. Guild members are mystified by the taxes, pointing out the role of the Guild and the High Wizard in maintaining the defences of the city.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{The Merchants’ Guild}

The drinking-room of this guild is always full of merchants and traders discussing this and that, and they happily talk about the taxes. They are not too bothered, for the most part: ‘Glad it wasn’t us’ is the usual attitude. The more thoughtful types, though, are concerned: ‘It’ll turn out badly. The Dwarfs are good workers and good spenders, and this will bring trouble.’ Several members suspect that the Chancellor is behind the taxes, especially the Scroll Tax. ‘Sort of thing he’d do. Problem with him is he doesn’t see the effects on people. Bit of a recluse, he is.’

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.CX77jCGRkysWfOKy]{The Dwarven Engineers’ Guild}

A similar response is seen here as at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.h1NmGWYdOpGvgrbg]{Komission for Elven, Dwarven, and Halfling Interests}. A petition is proffered, even if the Characters have signed it before. Nothing new can be learned over a few beers; the Dwarfs — mainly engineers and  artisans — spend most of their time moaning and making provisional plans to leave. There is some talk of ambushing either @UUID[Actor.nzNgV71abEH1iNFo]{Rallane} or the @UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Chancellor}, and making the Dwarf point of view known forcefully.

The Underworld

There is no centralised Thieves’ Guild in Middenheim, but most criminal activities are overseen by two powerful gangs, one based in Ostwald and the other in the Altquartier. The leaders of these gangs are known colloquially in Middenheim as the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.Liw9HcyJnHbLZevz]{Low Kings}. They vie with each other violently, and any criminal who seeks to operate in their territories without handing over a quota of their takings best keep their activities secret, unless they are forced at knifepoint to be more cooperative.

There are various ways of contacting the underworld. For example, a Thief (or other Rogue Character) might locate an NPC rogue by watching for signs of thieving on the streets — requiring a successful Difficult (+0) Observe Test, repeated every hour until successful — or an NPC thief might spot and approach a Character thief.

In the second case, the NPC makes a sign of recognition specific to Middenheim. When the Character fails to respond properly, the NPC will quietly point out that it might be a good idea to come along for a chat: after all, it’s difficult to pick a pocket without fingers, isn’t it?

After some preliminary sounding-out in which the locals will establish to their satisfaction that the Character is genuine and not in the pay of the authorities, a nocturnal meeting is arranged. The Character is offered provisional membership to cover Carnival week at a cost of a gold crown, and is then taught the local dialect of Thieves’ Tongue (the character must already have the basic Skill) and told about various contact points. If there is time for a solo adventure, the Character thief might be set a task as proof of ability and goodwill.

Questions about the taxes or the court is met with some puzzlement, but this is satisfied by any reasonably non-committal reply (‘just curiosity: it seems a bit odd’). The NPC thief casually mentions that he knows someone who can find out anything about anything, if the price is right. If the Character agrees, a further meeting is arranged in a secluded tavern some 12 hours later, for a [[/r d10+3]] shilling, ‘arrangement fee.’

At this meeting, the Character is introduced to ‘Josef,’ a shifty individual aged about 40, who never looks anyone in the eye. Josef collects and sells information for a living — he neither knows nor cares what any of it means, so long as he gets his fee ([@Pay[3ss]{3 schillings}, in advance, no haggling). He charges an additional fee (which he may try to bargain upwards, though usually about 2 shillings) for each piece of information he passes on. Josef never reveals his sources.

Josef ’s Knowledge

@UUID[Actor.nzNgV71abEH1iNFo]{Rallane} is probably not behind the Dwarf Tax. It is not his style, and he expressed surprise when it was introduced ([[/r d10]] shillings).

The Midden Marshals do not have as much influence as many people claim, and the @UUID[Actor.6yFVH9mzC5VoQAUh]{Knight Eternal} has none at all ([[/r 2d10]] shillings).

@UUID[Actor.2T8CXsP45Z3Kptvi]{Law Lord Ehrlich} was seen leaving the Palace visibly upset the day Graf Boris passed the new taxes. This coincided with the start of his current fit of depression ([[/r 5d10]] shillings).

After passing on this information, Josef develops an uneasy  look, and players may guess that he knows more. If pressed, helean forwards and say in a low voice:

‘All right, but putting this in the wrong ears could get you burnt or worse. @Pay[1gc]{A Crown} gets you something about Ar-Ulric — no messing about, yes or no?’ He can be bargained down to @Pay[10ss]{10 schillings}, and if an agreement is reached he says that Ar-Ulric has been seen leaving the apartments of the Ladies-at-Court late at night: ‘A bit naughty, that, considering his vow of celibacy and all.’

Josef may possess other pieces of information, if you wish. Their price can be based on the importance of the individual or group mentioned.

The Temples

Any Character priest who visits his or her temple in the city hears a good deal of complaint. The biggest question concerns the relationship between the Graf and the cult of Ulric. On the one hand, why would the Graf risk alienating them when the cult of Sigmar already regards him as a threat? On the other hand, why has the cult of Ulric not spoken out against the taxes, especially when High Priest Ar-Ulric is one of the Graf’s advisors?

Popular rumour is that, while they have a lot to lose, the cult of Ulric is the richest in the city, and plans to sit tight while pressure of taxation squeezes the others out.

There is no information on the origins of the taxes or the destination of the money raised, but the temples know that the taxes certainly do not reflect any popular anti-clerical feeling. If anything, the general population was as surprised as the groups affected.

Note: If the Character priest visit the temples of other deities, they should behave with the utmost respect and tact. In particular, the presence of a priest of Sigmar in the temple of Ulric (or vice-versa) could be seen as provocative.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.fvLZwi16FbG2gc7V]{The Temple Of Ulric}

@UUID[Actor.VqvKKvGm7y1XzDUe]{Ar-Ulric} is frequently absent on business, but his juniors, Franz Fassbinder and Gilda Heinzer, ensure that little is given away here. They are both excellent at deflecting questions. 

Even the junior priests say little. It is clear that the priests are not happy about the tax, but they do not condemn it in as forthright a manner as one might expect: a successful Challenging (+0) Intuition Test reveals that a priest interviewed here appears to be hesitant in what he or she is saying.

The priests of Ulric are in a difficult position: they cannot openly condemn the taxes without appearing to condemn their leader’s apparent failure to stop them, and yet they cannot speak in their favour either. Most try to skirt the issue, saying that such matters are not for ordinary folk to comment on; they may be more open with a character who wins their trust and approaches the question diplomatically.

If a Character priest of Ulric is able to gain an interview with Fassbinder or Heinzer (this takes 1-3 days to arrange, and only priests of Ulric are admitted) a successful Challenging (+0) Charm Test leads to their dropping a hint about their reasons for their relative lack of vigour in originally condemning the taxes: they must follow @UUID[Actor.VqvKKvGm7y1XzDUe]{Ar-Ulric’s} lead, and he has given no sign of his views on the matter: on an Impressive or better success, they say that he seems preoccupied lately, and he has been difficult to approach.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.r4Bd5zWLRdZPaOsj]{The Temple Of Sigmar}

Feelings run higher here than in the temple of Ulric, and, although the priests are rather tight-lipped, their anger is obvious. On a successful Challenging (+0) Gossip Test, a junior priest might forget himself so far as to accuse Ar-Ulric of supporting the tax to squeeze the other temples out of the city; on an Impressive or better success, he may even question whether the temple of Ulric is actually paying the Temple Tax.

The priests of Sigmar also feel that the Dwarf Tax is a deliberate slight on their cult, given the historical links between the cult of Sigmar and the Dwarven people.

High Capitular @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.r4Bd5zWLRdZPaOsj]{Werner Stolz} (a High Priest of Sigmar) is not available to meet with the Characters, but they can learn that he met with the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.actors.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist} privately during his recent visit, and denounced both @UUID[JournalEntry.i9Ilr6BOGtcBQaCg.JournalEntryPage.lRSw5AXY7qM7QUnO]{Ar-Ulric} and @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} in no uncertain terms. Needless to say, this does nothing to reduce the current tension between the Empire’s two greatest religions.

A character who makes sympathetic noises in all the right places, or who is a follower of Sigmar, may be rewarded by a priest forgetting himself for a moment, and letting slip the news that Stolz is setting off for Altdorf after the Carnival, to put his case to the Emperor in person. This is clearly very sensitive information, and careless talk only make matters worse. This news should also lead them to realise that if anything is to be done about the tax changes, it must be done before the end of Carnival week.

GM Option: Dropping Names

A visit to the Temple of Ulric offers the GM a chance to have the Characters meet two NPCs — one is destined for greatness, the other for notoriety — but at present they are still relatively obscure. For the players, a chance meeting with a character whose name they recognise can make a lasting impression.

If you prefer not to use these characters, or to save them for another point in the campaign, that is quite permissible. They might be posted to temples away from Middenheim at the moment, eagerly awaiting the promotions that will bring them back to the City of the White Wolf, and one step closer to making history.

The Temple Of Shallya

The Characters are able to encounter junior priests fairly easily, but need a good reason to gain an appointment with the High Priestess, @UUID[Actor.0hUeYuOTIij6fMt4]{Isolde Begegnen}.

Here, the priests denounce the Temple Tax openly: it is taking money which would have helped the poor and sick, and putting it in the Graf ’s coffers. The Dwarf and Scroll Taxes are aimed at some of their more generous contributors, making matters worse. The temple is simple, and clearly keeps little of the money it receives — unlike some.

The temple of Shallya also resents Ar-Ulric’s lack of action — he is supposed to represent all temple interests in court circles, and has clearly failed them on this occasion. Some Sigmarites have over-reacted badly, accusing Ar-Ulric of plotting with the Graf to get rid of them: this is clearly ridiculous, since the @UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.LHLPCNetl8UKzaXx]{Temple Tax} affects the temple of Ulric as much as any other in the city.

The Characters might come here if they need healing, so Isolde Begegnen’s profile is given below: she may or may not treat injured Characters in person, but her profile indicates what is available if they are in serious need. A donation is not obligatory, but would be very much appreciated.

Religion.name: Religion
Religion.text:
Having heard various rumours on the way to Middenheim, the Characters may well try to learn more about the growing tension between the cults of Sigmar and Ulric.

The Sigmarian Heresy

Every Middenheimer, and almost everyone in Middenland and the north, has at least heard of the heresy — or as most Ulricans call it, ‘the controversy’. Put simply and shockingly, it proposes that Sigmar’s divinity is second to Ulric’s — if it even exists at all! They argue strongly that Sigmar was mortal and only became Emperor with the Ar-Ulric’s  blessing. It was only after his disappearance that Sigmar became a god. They conclude from this that Sigmar is less divine than Ulric, more of a warrior saint than a true god.

Theologians have grappled with this conundrum for centuries, with many heated debates at various councils (in particular, the Council of Nuln and the Council of Tilea): warrior saint, demigod, or deity? Until recently it was regarded more as an exercise in logic — a paradox for students and initiates to study — than as a serious indictment of the Empire’s most powerful religion. But now, a growing and vocal faction of fundamentalist Ulricans has begun to embrace it, claiming that it calls into question the legitimacy of the Emperor’s rule, and that of all Sigmar’s successors.

The Sons of Ulric

The @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{Sons of Ulric} are a loose and disorganised confederation of religious fanatics, northern separatists, bigots, and thugs bound together by the common belief that a blood descendant of Ulric ought to lead the official cult. It is no surprise then to learn that many prominent Sons of Ulric go so far as to claim to be blood descendants of Ulric themselves, and invoke their supposed ancestry to justify acts of sedition and violence. The group has no overall leader, central organisation, or coherent agenda.

There have been a number of activities attributed to the Sons of Ulric, including calls for the north to separate from the more Sigmarite south, breaking the Empire into two separate nations. Discrimination against followers of Sigmar ranging from refusing to do business with them to attacks on their temples, homes, and persons is on the increase. Other factors that add to the rising tensions are advocating for laws and taxes that target followers of Sigmar specifically; civil disobedience toward officials from Altdorf; and blaming them for any crime, disaster, or public mishap. They have little love for the official cult, saying that it is weak and that Ar-Ulric ought to be chosen from their own ranks.

Ar-Ulric has publicly called for calm and tolerance, and the group is technically banned from holding assemblies in Middenheim, but he has stopped short of criticising the group’s anti-Sigmarite stance — something that followers of Sigmar see as significant. The Graf has condemned the growing lawlessness and violence, and has increased taxes to pay for more watchmen, but he has not disavowed the Sons of Ulric or taken any action against them specifically.

The Grand Theogonist

A few weeks ago the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.actors.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist}, the leader of the Sigmarite faith, visited Middenheim for talks with the Graf and Ar-Ulric. Although this is not unprecedented in itself, he was accompanied by a much larger escort than usual, which included witch hunters as well as Templars of the Fiery Heart.

The Characters may have encountered the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.actors.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist} and his entourage on the road, and have probably  heard of the recent activities of Sigmarite witch hunters in the city. The presence of such a strong force, and the witch hunters’ high-handed actions, caused considerable tension; although a strong Watch presence was able to prevent riots. Sons of Ulric have criticised the Graf for meekly allowing this Sigmarite force to enter the city freely and do as it pleased.

Followers of Sigmar are more conciliatory. They are grateful to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.actors.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist} for coming to Middenheim, and to the @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf} and @UUID[Actor.VqvKKvGm7y1XzDUe]{Ar-Ulric} for meeting with him. Although no official statements have been made about their discussions, the leaders of Middenheim’s Sigmarite community still hope for a peaceful resolution to the growing religious tensions — though some less optimistic souls are packing up and heading south toward Altdorf, counting their blessings (Sigmar’s or Ulric’s) to be free of whatever reckoning is certain to visit Middenehim soon.

North And South

The religious tensions have a significant regional dimension, going back to the tribes that Sigmar united to create the Empire, more than twenty-five hundred years ago. The cult of Ulric is the most powerful religion in the northern provinces, which were the territory of the Teutognens. Sigmar’s faith is strongest in the southern homeland of his Unberogen tribe, centred on Altdorf and the Reikland.

If they are Reiklanders, the Characters — the Humans in the party, at least — have almost certainly grown up with a degree of suspicion regarding those from other provinces. In Middenheim, they discover that they themselves are outsiders, and regarded with suspicion. It quickly becomes apparent to them that the Sons of Ulric are using regional differences as well as religious ones to justify their activities.

Even those Middenheimers who do not agree with the rhetoric and violence of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{Sons of Ulric} may privately admit that they may have a point when it comes to the question of north versus south. They may point out that there are many differences beside religion: northerners are hardier and less flighty than southerners; northern culture places more emphasis on personal integrity while southerners seem to regard profits as a legitimate justification for anything.

All of this, of course, is thinly disguised regional prejudice, which every Middenlander has to some degree, even if they are not consciously aware of it. If pressed, a great many Middenheimers admit that they would prefer for the Emperor to rule the south and @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} the north as co-regents. But a vocal minority claims that complete separation from the Empire would save the north so much in taxes that everyone would enjoy unprecedented prosperity, including the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{Sons of Ulric}.  

Refugees And Atrocities

The followers of Ulric and Sigmar have very different views on this subject, as might be expected. Most Ulricans believe that the reports of attacks on Sigmarites in Middenheim have been exaggerated, if not completely fabricated. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{The Sons of Ulric} maintain that they are lies spread by agents of the Emperor to justify a planned invasion of the north. The ultimate goal  of this planned invasion is to replace the Graf with an @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.Zt9cBtaoKEL2kjPF.JournalEntryPage.3P8zPUpg3HqowmDZ]{Imperial Plenipotentiary} from Altdorf in the role of viceroy, abolishing the post of Elector Count and bringing Middenland — and ultimately, the whole of the north — under the direct rule of an Emperor who would be accountable to no one.

While most Middenheimers believe that the numbers of Sigmarite refugees fleeing Middenland have also been exaggerated, some think the count may be accurate, and even take pleasure in the thought that these ‘southerners’ — for all that many are Middenheim born and bred — are leaving the city to the true Ulricans who belong there.

By contrast, every Sigmarite in Middenheim has a story to tell. Some, especially those who have come from out of town for the Carnival, report no more than occasional rudeness or jostling. But resident Sigmarites disagree with this entirely. They have either experienced discrimination or violence directly, or know someone who has. Tavern brawls and back-alley beatings have escalated to bricks through windows and daubed slogans; one or two suspicious fires have broken out in Sigmarite-owned homes and businesses; and everyone knows at least one family that has packed up and moved south.

A Dark Motive

@UUID[JournalEntry.mLb1D0szfsRK0ZOd.JournalEntryPage.LHLPCNetl8UKzaXx]{The Temple Tax} and the tax on priests entering the city have the greatest impact on the city’s religious community, and @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} has made sure that @Actor[VqvKKvGm7y1XzDUe]{Ar-Ulric} supports them.

The followers of other gods are outraged, and there are rumours — especially among the city’s Sigmarite community — that Ar-Ulric not only supports the taxes but suggested them, as part of an organised effort to force other religions out of the city: his cult has amassed great wealth from the city’s faithful and visiting pilgrims, and can outlast any of the others.

If the taxes are another weapon in the growing religious strife, then the Graf must be in favour of the suppression of other religions. It seems possible that they may be a prelude to other measures against Sigmar and Altdorf, culminating in the outright secession of Middenheim, Middenland, and much of the north. The Characters cannot be sure until they know more, but with the stakes potentially so high, they must find out the truth.

'RESTORING THE NORTH’ OR ‘TAKING BACK CONTROL’

A vocal minority state that in order to make Middenheim glorious again, the following need to be addressed. 

  • The burdensome regulations on trade cost the north a fortune in lost business.

  • Altdorf places the interests of the south, and the Reikland in particular, over those of the rest of the Empire.

  • Customs charges on luxury goods from the south would generate enormous revenue while not affecting the average northerner at all, enabling the Graf to lower Middenheim’s taxes to almost nothing.

  • Southerners and those of foreign lands in general, are flooding into the north at an unprecedented rate, taking jobs, forcing housing prices up, and dominating commerce to an extent that wil soon reduce true-prn Middenheimers to an underclass in their own city.

  • The controversial new taxes are only necessary because the Graf has to send so much money to Altdorf in taxes.

The Skaven.name: The Skaven
The Skaven.text:
On the way to Middenheim, the Characters may have heard rumours about giant rats and rat-headed Beastmen in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.cU4GPNeGxCPgm4hE]{Middenheim’s Undercity}. After their encounters with Skaven in Death on the Reik, they are probably interested in finding out more. However, this will not be as easy as they might expect.

To most people in the Old World, the Skaven are a myth. Although history records the Skaven Wars of 1,400 years ago, their activities since have been shrouded in secrecy. The Skaven take great care to destroy any evidence of their activities and kill any witnesses, lest their secret nests and tunnels beneath the Old World’s great cities should be discovered and a new series of wars ensue. Because of this, most in the Empire — especially in Middenheim, home of Count Mandred von Zelt, the legendary Ratslayer and greatest hero of the Skaven Wars — believe that the entire Skaven race was wiped out in the wars. Middenheimers  discount present-day sightings as the product of superstition and hysteria.

Therefore, characters asking about Skaven are likely to encounter scorn and disbelief, and even to be fed ridiculous lines of nonsense by NPCs who want to amuse themselves at the expense of these credulous out-of-towners. Other NPCs may react angrily to such inquiries, their civic pride offended by any suggestion that the ratmen could have escaped detection and extermination.

Those Who Know

If the Characters ask the right questions in the right places, though, they may come across someone who knows that the Skaven still exist. Those who know  can tell them tales of hair-raising encounters. After the Characters hear enough such tales, a pattern starts to emerge — but by then, the events of the Carnival and the machinations of the Purple Hand require all their attention. Further investigation will have to wait until The Horned Rat, in which the Characters will learn more about the dreaded ratmen than they ever wanted to know.

The Rat Catchers

If one wants to know about rats, of course, the best person to ask is a rat catcher. Middenheim’s rat catchers are licensed by the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.2QMwt6sDAfJ6Rjt1]{Komission for Health, Education, and Welfare}, which is based in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.t1wYBKV4LW8o0XJ1]{Neumarkt}-@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.pvuBkAdDt7cuaIud]{Osttor} district. Anyone who goes there talking about Skaven is dismissed as a crackpot. A more cautious approach, for example, an enquiry about the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.l5XoRjq9k4ZN7DXt]{Rat Catchers' Guild} by a prospective member, leads the Characters to @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dO8liJoG38qWZmYO]{the Regent's House} tavern off Schwanger Allee, where guild members meet in an upstairs room most evenings.

The rat catchers are reluctant to speak of such matters to outsiders, but a few successful Fellowship Tests, helped along by a liberal quantity of ale, may establish trust enough to loosen a few tongues. The Characters may learn that rat-headed Beastmen are seen in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.cU4GPNeGxCPgm4hE]{Undercity} now and again, although no one sober concedes that they are Skaven; they may also confirm the rumours of giant rats.

The Sewer Jacks

In the aftermath of the Skaven Wars Middenheim’s sewer jacks were established as a special arm of the City Watch  to patrol the Undercity and deal with any threats that might come up from below. Enquiries at any of the city gates lead the Characters to the Watch office on the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.Non5YhyYgrHDW6mB]{Square of Martials}. A Character with at least one warrior or rat catcher career can pose as a potential recruit, and be introduced to the leader of the sewer jacks, a tough-looking Halfling named Jacko Warble.

Again, some Fellowship Tests are needed to establish a level of trust where the Characters can ask about Skaven without being laughed out of the building. But a sewer jack may confirm that Skaven — or creatures very like Skaven — have been encountered in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.cU4GPNeGxCPgm4hE]{Undercity}, though the sewer jacks have been unable to discover how they get in and out, as they are fond of collapsing tunnels behind them to prevent pursuit.

The Dwarfs

The city’s Dwarven community knows the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.cU4GPNeGxCPgm4hE]{Undercity} better than almost any other group. Dwarf @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.h1NmGWYdOpGvgrbg]{Komission for Elven, Dwarven, and Halfling} Interests may put the Characters in touch with local Dwarf leaders, and Dwarfs who ask at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.CX77jCGRkysWfOKy]{Dwarven Engineers’ Guild}, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.lVcFVQgg0OF2sti5]{Temple of Grungni}, or anywhere else associated with the Dwarven community will be directed to Modi Zargul at the Axe and Barrel Tavern in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.ff6FiBZzU2RippS1]{the Wynd}. The place caters to a Dwarven clientele: its ceilings are 5’ 6”” high, counting as an enclosed space for Humans and Elves; all non-Dwarfs suffer a –10 penalty to Fellowship Tests; and there is a 75% chance that any Dwarf NPC encountered here has @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.0VpT5yubw4UL7j6f]{Animosity} toward Elves.

Modi is one of several Ironbreakers in Middenheim, and admits to a fellow Dwarf that he sometimes leads unofficial patrols through the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.cU4GPNeGxCPgm4hE]{Undercity} on the orders of the Dwarf elders. He and his Ironbreakers have encountered Skaven, and are in no doubt that the creatures do exist: ‘but if the Manlings like to think otherwise, that’s their business. We just kill them when we find them.’

The Skaven Plot

The Skaven-worshipping Yellow Fang cult is well established in Middenheim. They have infiltrated organisations such as the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.PJSTe8IXwh6oy78t]{Collegium Theologica}, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.l5XoRjq9k4ZN7DXt]{Rat Catchers' Guild}, the Sewer Jacks, and various Komissions. The Yellow Fang monitors the organisations it infiltrates for news of any threat to its masters in the Under-Empire. The cult generates a constant stream of misleading rumour to help obscure Skaven activities.

The Skaven themselves are not unusually active in the city at present, with the exception of the group that kidnapped Reya, @UUID[Actor.2T8CXsP45Z3Kptvi]{Law Lord Ehrlich’s} niece (see @UUID[JournalEntry.yXOEsyeWgRgbeVmc.JournalEntryPage.QBR9vcY928EotGA2]{Chaos Strikes By Night}) Success here helps the Characters free Ehrlich from Wasmeier’s control, and set the adventure’s finale in motion.

However, the Skaven are not a major part of this adventure, and the players should realise quite quickly that there are other things afoot. If the players become obsessed with the Skaven, you may indulge them if you wish. However, be sure to have NPCs remind them that events involving the Carnival, the taxes, and growing sectarian discontent continue to build quite apart from what any large rats in the sewers may be plotting.

IN THE SHADOW OF THE HORNED RAT

While the role of the Skaven is limited in Power Behind the Throne, the species of devious rat-creatures that plagues the Empire, often quite literally, will feature heavily in The Horned Rat, part four of The Enemy Within. If you intend to run that adventure in the future then NPCs informed of Skaven activities, especially @UUID[Actor.jBamTcOi8iz3mYxe]{Ulrich Schutzmann}, may give the Characters' tales of humanoid rats some consideration. They will also make it clear, however, that any serious investigation will have to wait until after the Carnival has concluded.

Parting Ways.name: Hora de separarse
Parting Ways.text:
Al final de @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.w5rvSKCXvivjnTVU]{Muerte en el Reik}, los PJs acaban de llegar a Altdorf, contratados para llevar una caja a la Ciudad del Lobo Blanco. Hay muchas cosas que les tientan en la vasta y bulliciosa capital, pero deben darse prisa si quieren entregar la carga a tiempo y cobrar el dinero prometido.

Hora de separarse

Según hayan sido los acontecimientos anteriores, el grupo tendrá que realizar algunas despedidas.

La Barcaza

En @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.fzxPnClojPBcpfmA]{‘Un alto en el camino’}, el capítulo final de Muerte en el Reik, el DJ tenía varias opciones (algunas duras, otras no tanto) para asegurarse de que los PJs dejasen de tener una barcaza y, por lo tanto, no se vieran tentados de ignorar Middenheim y pasarse el resto de la vida subiendo y bajando por el Reik como comerciantes. Si todavía tienen su propia barcaza al comienzo de esta aventura, merece la pena reiterar algunas de estas opciones.

La ley del río

Al acercarse a Altdorf, la patrulla fluvial detiene el barco de los PJs para un control rutinario. La patrulla lo identifica como propiedad de otra persona: los parientes más cercanos de los anteriores dueños del barco (a quienes encontraron muertos a bordo de la embarcación a la deriva después de un ataque mutante, véase @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.49qp95QA3aWDRmWS.JournalEntryPage.kPzNtgpjZjwtHPpd]{‘Un barco en apuros’}) han denunciado la desaparición de la barcaza. Dado que está registrada en Altdorf, la patrulla fluvial de esa ciudad ha estado buscándola desde entonces.

Un DJ cruel puede ver al grupo acusado de asesinato y piratería, y exigirles que demuestren que encontraron el barco a la deriva y que se hicieron con él mediante un salvamento legal: @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.JPH3aDjaHPMg9sps]{Josef Quartjin} y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.wwwoy9PIIDOQZdF8]{Renate Hausier} declararán ser testigos de ello, si es que logran encontrarlos, o quizás un PJ o PNJ litigante tenga que demostrar su inocencia ante un magistrado, lo que requerirá Chequeos Prolongados de Sabiduría académica (derecho), Animar (discursos), y/o de cualquier otra habilidad que el DJ considere pertinente.

Una opción más amable, y más rápida, es suponer que la patrulla da por buena la historia de los PJs y que, según la costumbre del río, toda la carga y los beneficios de la embarcación les pertenecen por derecho de salvamento; y sólo insistirá en que el barco se entregue a los legítimos herederos del difunto propietario.

Un amigo en apuros

El viejo conocido y mentor de los PJs, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.JPH3aDjaHPMg9sps]{Josef Quartjin}, es un habitual en los muelles de Altdorf, así que no se sorprenden al encontrarlo en una taberna del puerto. Esta vez, sin embargo, la suerte no lo acompaña: su querida barcaza, el Berebeli, ha quedado destruida en un reciente ataque de mutantes o piratas del río o en una colisión con otra embarcación ‘tripulada por idiotas’, como dice Josef.

A menos que encuentre otro barco, Josef debe enrolarse como tripulante a las órdenes de otro patrón –una humillación casi insoportable para un barquero de su vasta experiencia– o sentarse en los muelles y ver cómo se agota el poco dinero que le queda. Al enterarse de que los PJs piensan ir a Middenheim, Josef aprovecha la oportunidad de hacerse cargo de su barcaza y promete conservarla en buen estado y repartir los beneficios con ellos cuando vuelvan.

Lo inesperado

Si los personajes salvaron la barcaza de ser pasto de las llamas en @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.fzxPnClojPBcpfmA]{‘Un alto en el camino’} es posible que no esperen que el incendiario vuelva a atacar de nuevo, pero tal vez se equivoquen. Su cliente @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.FTT9hoFswIqAW9do]{Matthias Blucher} mandará quemar el barco en Altdorf tan pronto como le den la espalda.

Si todavía llevaban una carga con destino a Marienburgo, la perderán, sin que haya ninguna cláusula en el contrato que diga que la familia Blucher pagará las reparaciones. Sin embargo, los agentes de Blucher en la capital les ofrecerán el encargo menos remunerado de llevar una gran caja al capitán Scharlach en Middenheim (ver @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.w5rvSKCXvivjnTVU.JournalEntryPage.ZQQPvOQxMQ4YrExI#misfortune-managed]{‘La gestión de la desgracia’}) si no han aceptado ya el trabajo.

En el mercado

Como alternativa, cabe la posibilidad de que los PJs decidan vender la barcaza, que vale, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.g796u6AgEQvRPlp7]{al menos en teoría}, 225 CO. Por supuesto, vender una barcaza no es tan sencillo como aceptar una bolsa de dinero y marcharse del muelle: hay que completar un papeleo para transferir la propiedad y actualizar los registros oficiales y se debe tener en cuenta la antigüedad y el estado de la embarcación, la cantidad de barcos similares que hay en el mercado local y el número de personas interesadas en comprar.

A menos que los PJs tengan la intención de permanecer en Altdorf al menos una semana –y renuncien entregar el paquete a tiempo en Middenheim– harían bien en poner el asunto en manos de un intermediario. En Altdorf y otros grandes puertos de río abundan mercaderes especializados que se encargan de todos los detalles de la compra o venta de un barco a cambio de un 10% del precio. Hay que tener en cuenta que otro 5 % se va en concepto de tasas de documentación, amarres, impuestos y otros gastos.

¡Guárdanos este dichoso trasto!

Puede que algunos jugadores quieran quedarse la barcaza a pesar de todo lo que intentes para privarles de ella, y es poco probable que renuncien a ella sólo porque hayan contratado los PJs para ir a Middenheim. A menos que hagan algo extravagante, como ponerle ruedas al barco y llevarlo por carretera, deberán dejarlo en Altdorf y hacer alguna provisión de fondos para cuidarlo hasta que regresen a recobrarlo.

Si ésta es la única manera de poner a los PJs en el camino a Middenheim, que así sea. Si bien hay que tener en cuenta los gastos de guarda y custodia, trata de que sean comedidos para que no se apresuren a regresar de Middenheim antes de que tengan la oportunidad de involucrarse en la trama de El Poder tras el Trono. Unas pocas monedas de plata a la semana serán más que suficiente. Si tienes el Compendio de Muerte en el Reik, recuerda a los jugadores que un tiempo en un dique seco de Altdorf podría ser una excelente oportunidad para aplicar @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.FtADtP0t2I9PBiSa]{mejoras} a su querida barcaza. Si tienes la intención de continuar con La Rata Cornuda, será muy probable que pase algún tiempo antes de que se les presente la oportunidad de volver a la embarcación.

Y, si de verdad es necesario, siempre cabe la posibilidad de que vuelvan para encontrarse todo el dique seco en llamas. Por suerte y en caso de necesidad, ¡nunca faltan un par de pirómanos en Altdorf!

Alex se va a Middenheim

Si los PJs han llegado a Altdorf a bordo del Salmón Azul, se separarán de @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.Pa77IT9maJR1nU7M]{Alex Eisen} y su tripulación. 

Alex está entusiasmado por ir al carnaval de Middenheim. ‘No me lo perdería por nada’ dice, con su habitual estilo brusco y fanático. ‘Esos norteños son más aburridos que una ostra en cualquier otra época del año, pero, si les das unos cuantos vasos de coñac en el carnaval, ¡cuidado! Oh, sí, sí, ¿sabes a lo que me refiero?’ A no ser que haya terminado a malas con los PJs, sugerirá que viajen juntos: ‘Cuantos más seamos, mejor, ya sabéis, y, aparte de los hombres bestia del bosque, es útil tener a alguien de confianza que te cubra las espaldas en una posada por la noche, por no mencionar que Middenheim está lleno de gente que te cortaría la garganta por el oro de tus dientes... No lo digo por vosotros, claro. Desde el principio supe que eráis de los buenos. De todos modos, esos elfos –ya sabéis a quiénes me refiero– nunca bajan la guardia, ¿Eh? ¿Eh? Sí, sí, nos entendemos’. Es probable que la mayoría de PJs prefieran evitarlo, así que deberán buscarse alguna excusa.

The Journey.name: El viaje
The Journey.text:
El viaje de Altdorf a Middenheim es de más de 350 millas: suponiendo que los PJs vayan en diligencia, se tarda seis días en total. Los puntos de parada habituales en el camino son los siguientes.

Etapas entre Altdorf y Middenheim
DíaEtapaDistancia
1Altdorf – Frederheim – Kutenholz63 millas
2Kutenholz – El Hogar del Bosque – Bröckel65 millas
3Bröckel – Mittelweg*58 millas
4Mittelweg – Delberz – Sotturm64 millas
5Sotturm – Malstedt – Grubentreich66 millas 
6Grubentreich – Schoninghagen – Middenheim46 millas

* No hay parada de mediodía en esta etapa: en vez de ello, la posada de Bröckel proporciona vituallas a todos los pasajeros.

Las paradas

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.mbXVJGCGSm8m7ANd.JournalEntryPage.U1AyyYhJ5Oqyb6VP]{La posada La Diligencia y los Caballos (El Enemigo en las Sombras)} puede utilizarse como modelo para cualquier casa de postas a lo largo del camino, cambiando el diseño a tu discreción. El personal que las atiende puede convertirse en personajes nuevos con sólo cambiarles el nombre y un poco la personalidad.

Frederheim

Más conocido como el hogar del Gran Hospicio de Shallya (que en realidad se encuentra fuera del pueblo, en lo más profundo del bosque), Frederheim no tiene más que la posada La Paloma (independiente) y un puñado de tiendecitas que han crecido para atender sus necesidades y albergar un mercado quincenal para las granjas de los alrededores.

Kutenholz

Kutenholz es la primera parada en Middenland. Cuenta con una posada llamada La Cabeza del Lobo y un gran santuario de Ulric en las cercanías. La Cabeza del Lobo luce con orgullo el emblema de @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.MomqBNXC7pOwzeue]{Roca del Castillo}. Aunque su personal no rechaza las diligencias de otras compañías, las de Roca del Castillo reciben un trato preferente. Este trato incluye algunas pequeñas ventajas, como ser los primeros en elegir habitaciones, un 10% de descuento en la comida y el alojamiento y una bebida de cortesía por llegar a Middenland.

El Hogar del Bosque

Esta posada fortificada se encuentra al pie del camino, con nada más que bosque a ambos lados. Sus muros tienen más de 6 pies de altura y estacas en la parte superior. Los ataques de los hombres bestia a la posada en sí no son comunes, pero los ataques a las diligencias que vienen y van se han vuelto más comunes en los últimos, sobre todo al norte. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.XGUpnYfS67guNIWJ.JournalEntryPage.R2BCxi4CJH4hUrru#four-seasons-coaches]{Las Cuatro Estaciones} ha hecho varios intentos de hacerse con ella, ya que es el único alojamiento entre Kutenholz y Bröckel. Esta ubicación les daría una ventaja importante respecto a la competencia. Sin embargo y hasta ahora, sus esfuerzos han sido en vano, y la posada sigue siendo de propiedad y gestión independientes.

Bröckel

Esta es un pueblecito sin importancia que sirve de mercado para los pueblos cercanos de Kupfengrube y Guthugel. La posada Las Armas de Bröckel, en el extremo sur del pueblo, es propiedad de Cuatro Estaciones. Los pasajeros de otras compañías deben recurrir a la más pequeña, pero más céntrica, Posada del Mercado. Construida para alojar a los agricultores locales que visitan el mercado mensual, suele tener de cuatro a cinco habitaciones y una docena de dormitorios libres cuando no hay feria.

Mittelweg

La Casa a Medio Camino es una de las posadas más antiguas del camino entre Altdorf y Middenheim. Su amplio muro circundante luce aún las cicatrices de los ataques de las fuerzas del Caos de hace dos siglos. Llamada así por su ubicación, a mitad de camino entre Altdorf y Middenheim, Mittelweg (NdC: literalmente, ‘mitad del camino’) creció alrededor de la gran casa con sus distintivos torreones, que ahora dan la bienvenida a los cansados viajeros. Se encuentran en cada esquina y sus dos pisos superiores cuentan con troneras.

La Casa a Medio Camino se enorgullece de su historia y emplazamiento, y su personal se enorgullece de la cálida acogida que dispensan. Cada noche se celebra una ‘velada de mitad del camino’ para los viajeros, con una buena (aunque costosa) comida, bebidas gratis y recuerdos, incluidas sus novedosos medios vasos y jarras de media pinta. Estas jarras y vasos parecen de tamaño normal por un lado, pero son planos por el otro, como si estuvieran cortados por la mitad de arriba a abajo. Normalmente se llevan a la mesa por pares, con pinzas de madera para sujetar las dos mitades.

De nuevo en el camino

El viaje al norte es una oportunidad para preparar a los jugadores para Middenheim. El clima se vuelve más frío, los viajeros que pasan parecen más sombríos, las diferencias religiosas y culturales se hacen más palpables y los (@UUID[.5KNnpHmwPu4zJUdO]{rumores}) abundan a medida que los PJs se enteran de los problemas de la ciudad.
