News and Rumours.name: Noticias y rumores
News and Rumours.text:
Noticias y rumores

Estas habladurías pueden escucharse a lo largo del camino, en cualquiera de las diversas paradas del mismo o en boca de los compañeros de viaje. Tira un [[/r d10]] para elegir al azar o elige un rumor apropiado para el PNJ en cuestión. Mientras que los rumores de luchas e impuestos en Middenheim sirven para ambientar el resto de la aventura, asegúrate de especiarlos también con algunas noticias de disturbios civiles en el Imperio. Estas te irán bien para presentar los hechos de La Rata Cornuda y El Imperio en Ruinas, los dos últimos capítulos de El Enemigo Interior.

  • Mientras Ostland y Talebecland están al borde de una guerra abierta, la rebelión se gesta en Middenland. La tolerancia del Emperador con los mutantes ha enfurecido a los feroces hijos de Ulric, y ahora los más devotos de ellos quieren expulsar a todos los demás sacerdotes de Middenheim para convertirla en una ciudad sólo de Ulric.

  • El Emperador ha reunido en palacio a todos sus comandantes para discutir los problemas en Middenheim. También ha exigido que el Graf Boris Todbringer, el Conde Elector de Middenheim, se reúna con él en la capital de inmediato.

  • El infame decreto de los mutantes del Emperador es un intento de evitar la guerra abierta con Middenheim. Porque todo el mundo sabe que los hombres bestia del Drakwald fueron una vez tan humanos como el propio Graf Boris. La mutación se extiende por la provincia como si fuera obra de alguna extraña influencia.

  • Las ratas de las alcantarillas de Middenheim no son como las que hay al sur. Miden 6 pies de largo, y algunas de ellas caminan erguidas, llevan ropa y hablan entre ellas con chillidos y parloteos. Los cazadores de ratas de Middenheim se ganan el sueldo, sin duda.

  • Los mutantes y los bandidos siguen atacando a las diligencias que cruzan el Drakwald. Las principales compañías contratan más protección y los Guardas de caminos están reclutando a hombres en Altdorf y los alrededores, pero el Emperador no ha enviado tropas para proteger la carretera. Mientras tanto, el aluvión de refugiados que marchan de Middenheim está a merced de bandidos y hombres bestia.

  • Los seguidores de Ulric son cada vez más militantes. No contentos con perseguir a los honestos y devotos sigmaritas, ahora empiezan a meterse con los sacerdotes de cualquier otro dios e incluso con los enanos, que ayudaron a construir Middenheim. Se han aprobado una serie de leyes fiscales ruinosas, dirigidas en concreto a los elfos, enanos, hechiceros y sacerdotes.

  • Todos estos impuestos nuevos sólo pueden significar una cosa: que el Graf está llenando sus arcas para contratar a tropas y mercenarios. Puede que se prepare para intervenir en el creciente conflicto entre Ostland y Talebecland o puede que pretenda romper relaciones con el Emperador y fortificar las orillas del norte del Reik y el Talabec contra las agresiones del sur.

  • Se está difundiendo una herejía que afirma que Sigmar nunca fue un dios, sólo un héroe mortal al que coronó emperador el sumo sacerdote de Ulric. Afirman que Ulric es el verdadero dios del Imperio y que los adoradores de Sigmar son herejes. La tensión entre el norte y el sur va y viene, pero todo el malestar parece estar girando en torno a las diferencias religiosas. Algunos fanáticos de Ulric quieren incluso que el norte rompa con el resto del Imperio y se convierta en una nación separada.

  • El Ar-Ulric no ha hecho ninguna declaración sobre la herejía o las actividades de esos bandidos fanáticos que se hacen llamar ‘Hijos de Ulric’. Por supuesto, ha condenado sus sugerencias de que piense en abdicar para que uno de ellos lo sustituya. Ha dicho que su creencia de que descienden de Ulric es muy apócrifa, y apoya al Graf en la prohibición de que se reúnan públicamente en la ciudad, pero, cuando se trata de las persecuciones a sigmaritas en Middenland, bien que cierra la boca.

  • La suegra del primo del que esto cuenta es lavandera en el castillo Reikguard. Dice haber visto al príncipe heredero Wolfgang, el cual parecía ‘más un lobo que otra cosa, ya entiendes lo que quiero decir’.

Los PJs pueden ir recopilando la información siguiente en la ciudad, ya sea mediante conversaciones con los habitantes de Middenheim o poniendo la oreja en conversaciones ajenas. Nota: debe ser creíble que los PNJs en cuestión hayan podido escuchar la información que transmiten. Por ejemplo, ningún mugriento campesino local sabe de las lejanas maquinaciones imperiales, mientras que es poco probable que los educados mercaderes o miembros de gremios educados cuenten meras supersticiones.

Algunos de estos rumores son la continuación de historias que es posible que el grupo haya oído durante @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.49qp95QA3aWDRmWS.JournalEntryPage.5KxxSWNDw2D0yyFS#news-and-rumours]{Muerte en el Reik}. Cuando sea necesario, el DJ deberá completar cualquier detalle que falte de las historias anteriores y que los PJs hayan pasado por alto.

El Imperio

A pesar de su actitud a veces adusta, a los habitantes de Middenheim les encanta cotillear, en especial respecto a las costumbres laxas de los que no son de Middenland y sobre todo durante el carnaval. Tira [[/r 1d10]] o elige un rumor apropiado para cada situación.

  • El estado de salud del emperador Karl-Franz es crítico. Su enfermedad ha sido de conocimiento público durante algún tiempo, pero ahora parece que se ha deteriorado. Los físicos de la corte han estado cooperando con los Colegios de la Magia, pero no han logrado descubrir la naturaleza de su enfermedad. ¿Y quién se ocupa de los asuntos importantes del estado durante esta crisis? Nadie. El descontento en la capital va en aumento, y se extiende por las provincias incluso mientras hablamos.

  • El Gran Duque Gustav von Krieglitz de Talabecland ha enviado emisarios al palacio del Gran Príncipe Hals von Tasseninck de Ostland. El duque niega la acusación de asesinato del hijo de von Tasseninck, Hans. También está enfadado por los recientes ataques a sus patrullas fronterizas por parte de los soldados del príncipe.

  • Han enviado al Barón Heinrich en una importante misión diplomática. Se dirige a Wolfenburgo para tratar de hacer entrar en razón a los von Tasseninck. He oído que va a pedirles que retiren cualquier insinuación de que von Krieglitz le hizo daño al hijo del príncipe heredero. Es una situación difícil, pero si alguien puede sacar a Talabecland y Ostland de una guerra, es nuestro Heinrich.

  • La Blitztruppen de Baumann, una unidad mercenaria de élite, ha estado reclutando nuevos miembros para una misión desconocida al este del Imperio. El propio Baumann se fue de la ciudad hace semanas. Nadie sabe si esto tiene algo que ver con el repentino aumento del robo de ganado, la quema de cultivos y las incursiones para cortar los transportes en la frontera de Ostland. La milicia local de allí está preocupada por el súbito aumento de los refugiados, dado el creciente ciclo de asaltos y represalias.

  • El edicto del Emperador que prohíbe dar muerte o exiliar a los mutantes en el Imperio no ha tenido una buena acogida. Han colgado a algunos aldeanos por asesinato según la nueva ley. Hace sólo un par de semanas, los aldeanos de Reikland se sublevaron después de que se condenara a un posadero por matar a un huésped al que le descubrieron escamas en la espalda.

  • El principal representante de la Asociación de Agricultores de Middenland, Dietrich Hoffman, pasó por aquí el otro día. Hizo una declaración ante el concejo, pronosticando lo peor para la cosecha de este año. Al parecer, las previsiones de cosecha parecen ser las mismas en todo el Imperio. Este año el clima es el culpable: demasiado frío en invierno; demasiado húmedo en primavera, o eso dicen. Pero los campesinos siempre se quejan, y nadie recuerda la última vez que hicieron una previsión precisa.

  • Marienburgo parece ser el mejor lugar para un comerciante en este momento. El negocio va en auge, y parece que seguirá aumentando en los próximos meses. El puerto funciona casi a pleno rendimiento, y los pedidos de grano de Bordeleaux están en un nivel nunca visto.

  • La cadena de torres de señales del Emperador traza un patrón muy siniestro en el mapa. Un primo del cuñado de la persona que cuenta esto trabaja limpiando la casa de un hechicero y ha visto un par de cosas. Algo malo sucederá cuando terminen dicha cadena, algo muy, pero que muy malo.

  • Se han visto carros entrando en el castillo Reikguard más a menudo de lo habitual, y en mayor número. Está claro que el Príncipe Heredero hace acopio de víveres y municiones.¡Se están preparando para una rebelión!

  • Eso es otra ‘conspiranoia’ estúpida e irresponsable. En realidad, lo que debe de estar haciendo es prepararse para apoyar al Emperador para atacar Middenland.

Middenheim

La Ciudad del Lobo Blanco puede ser un lugar desconocido y a veces extraño, pero sus habitantes están muy orgullosos de vivir allí y siempre se muestran dispuestos a hablar de la ciudad, su historia y su gente. Elige [[/br 1d13]]{al azar}, o escoge un rumor apropiado que corra sobre la propia Middenheim.

  • Puede que las Iluminaciones anuales de los hechiceros no sean tan grandiosas como en años anteriores. El impuesto sobre los pergaminos ha sido una maniobra muy mala, y Peter Kramer, un popular hechicero que ha dirigido la exhibición anual de las Flechas Rojas durante años, ha dejado la ciudad.

  • ¿Te has fijado en que más establecimientos enanos parecen cerrar desde que se introdujo el impuesto a los enanos? Lo raro es que han visto a pocos enanos saliendo, ya sea por el remonte o por las carreteras principales. Algunos dicen que se han escondido en los antiguos túneles bajo la ciudad.

  • ¿Has visto cómo se tratan los sacerdotes de Sigmar y Ulric entre ellos desde hace un tiempo? Hace unos días, se produjo una pelea fuera de Las Armas del Templario cuando algunos sacerdotes de Sigmar culparon al Sumo Sacerdote de Ulric por introducir el impuesto sobre templos.

  • Las defensas de la ciudad no son tan fuertes como la gente supone. Se ha prestado demasiada atención a los dudosos beneficios de la magia. Los enanos las están socavando de todos modos con sus túneles. Al menos, los hechiceros están recibiendo su merecido, ahora que los militares se dan cuenta de lo poco que han servido.

  • Si quieres ganar algo de dinero fácil en los próximos días, dedícate a tocar en la calle. Durante el carnaval, cualquiera con un violín y algo de voz puede ganar lo suficiente para vivir.

  • Estos nuevos impuestos se han introducido para que el Graf pueda montar una campaña contra el Emperador. Al parecer, el reciente edicto sobre los mutantes ha convencido al Graf Boris de que el viejo Karl-Franz chochea.

  • Pronto querrán un nuevo Señor de la Ley si el viejo Ehrlich no se recupera. Éste debe de ser su tercer ataque de melancolía desde que asumió el cargo. Me sorprende que Hoflich no se haya querido deshacer de él. Hoflich, no es el tipo más compasivo del mundo, que digamos.

  • La semana pasa hubo unos cazadores de brujas de Altdorf por aquí. Quemaron a diecisiete personas en la hoguera por ser adoradores del Caos y brujas. ¿Por qué la gente del Graf necesita a los sureños para esto? ¿No son capaces de erradicar a los seguidores del Caos ellos mismos? Los del Emperador no confían en nosotros para mantener nuestra propia casa en orden. Esos cazadores de brujas habrían estado igual de contentos quemando a los ulricanos de pro, sino más.

  • Alguien de la corte del Emperador estuvo en Middenheim hace poco y se trajo un destacamento de caballeros del sur como guardaespaldas. Algunos dicen que fue el sumo sacerdote de Sigmar –o ‘Gran Teogonista’, con perdón de su eminencia–, que vino a hablar con el Ar-Ulric sobre todo este malestar religioso que se ha estado gestando. Ahora se han ido, y que les vaya bien, pero el Emperador haría mejor en olvidarse de la religión y tratar a los habitantes de Middenland con más respeto. Ulric llegó aquí antes que Sigmar, ¡todo el mundo lo sabe!

  • Los hombres bestia cada vez se acercan más a la ciudad. Es probable que se alimenten de los cadáveres que caen por el Acantilado de los Suspiros. Algunos de ellos han muerto en la Subciudad debido a los lucios de las alcantarillas y los cazarratas. Dicen que todos esos bichos tenían cabeza de rata, pero ¿tú te lo crees? Cuando las únicas herramientas que tienes son una pértiga y un terrier rabioso todo parece una rata.

  • Los enanos de Middenheim han diseñado un maravilloso aparato volador en agradecimiento por el santuario que la ciudad les ha proporcionado durante más de 2500 años. Hasta los enanos respetan ese tipo de historia. Lo llaman ‘dirigible’, es como un globo con una máquina de vapor atornillada. El Barón Heinrich lo ha recibido con cortesía y se lo ha llevado directamente a Ostland. Lástima que te perdiste el día que se fue: verlo a él y a un pequeño escuadrón de Caballeros Pantera elevándose en el aire fue algo magnífico. Claro está, tan pronto como se fue, cayeron los impuestos. Ahora los enanos quieren recuperar el globo.

  • Si yo fuera el Graf, contrataría a mercenarios para resolver esta farsa en la frontera. El Torreón de Latón, ¿te suena? Una cohorte de norscanos mutados, llamados ‘los Desgraciados’, se esconde allí desde la época de Magnus el Piadoso. Debería de ser fácil eliminarlos, pero la cosa se ha visto envuelta en la política. La familia Kärzburdger es dueña de esa tierra, y no permite que se tomen medidas decisivas. Dicen que el lugar está maldito y que es mejor contener el problema en lugar de ponerle fin. Montaron un piquete para que los Desgraciados se rindieran por hambre. Doscientos años más tarde, los norscanos siguen allí, y el piquete también.

  • Los Kärzburdger solían dirigir el cotarro en Middenheim, pero han decaído mucho en estos dos últimos siglos. El Graf Kärzburdger, que ya está muy viejo, ha dejado que el culto de Shallya se lo llevara cogido de la oreja, literalmente, una humillación que nunca olvidarán. Por suerte, tenemos la bendición de tener un gobernante como Boris Todbringer, que es firme como una roca. Ojalá tuviera más hijos legítimos.

Para aventureros

Siempre hay trabajo disponible para los que son hábiles con la espada y puede que sea una tarea adecuada para uno o más PJs. Nota: ten en cuenta que algunos de estos rumores pueden hacer que los aventureros se alejen de la trama principal, pero si se usan con sabiduría, pueden ponerlos en la dirección correcta. Tira [[/r 1d10]] y elige al azar si lo deseas, pero es aconsejable elegir un rumor apropiado para la partida.

  • ¿Quieres ganar algo de dinero extra? Pues olvídate de intentar entrar en la milicia. Después de lo sucedido tras la final de Snotbol del año pasado, que casi acaba en disturbios, Schutzmann ‘Cabeza de Hierro’ ya ha contratado a cuatrocientos hombres para ayudar a la policía de la ciudad. Dicen que se ha gastado casi todo el presupuesto de todo el año en la semana del carnaval.

  • ¿Te has enterado de que todos los enanos se van? Bueno, alguien tendrá que mantener todos esos túneles controlados, van a estar pidiendo a gritos soldados que no tengan miedo a la oscuridad, y a ser posible de poca estatura.

  • Si quieres probar la buena vida, se rumorea que el Graf Boris quiere casar a su hija lo antes posible (codazo, codazo).

  • Se está contratando a más Guardas de caminos para los viajes a Marienburgo, Erengrad y algunos pueblos costeros del norte. Las cosas nunca son perfectas, pero las carreteras empeoran cada día. Este mes, ya van dos veces que no llega un cargamento de vodka kislevita.

  • ¿Tienes alguna experiencia en la caza de ratas? ¿Has visto lo gordas y hermosas que están ahora? ¿Quieres saber por qué? Los enanos han estado almacenando comida en esos túneles suyos, y las ratas la han encontrado.

  • Algunas personas muy acomodadas visitan Middenheim durante el carnaval, y la mayoría quiere contratar a guías y guardias. Las oportunidades de hacer dinero son buenas, y más desde que la Guardia de la ciudad está tan escasa de fondos que no se puede permitir más hombres.

  • Te diré una forma rápida de ganar una o dos coronas. Vístete como uno de la Guardia y llama a la puerta de algún noble exigiéndole impuestos. Si lo haces a primera hora de la mañana, te daría hasta a su hija antes que despertarse.

  • Esta es buena: algunos jóvenes creen que el Canciller Sparsam saca tajada de los nuevos impuestos y guarda el dinero en su casa. Calculan que se ha embolsado cinco mil coronas. Pero tendrás suerte si acabas encontrando cinco peniques siquiera: Sparsam es tan avaro que guarda todas las monedas en un lugar que ni el mismo Ranald puede conseguir meter mano.

  • Dicen que el Barón Stefan está mejorando. Sólo Ulric sabe lo que ese doktor loco le está administrando… como si no estuviera medio muerto por estar atiborrado de cataplasmas. ¿Qué más se podría hacer con él?

  • Si sabes leer y escribir bien, consigue un trabajo en la Komission Tributaria. Con todos estos impuestos nuevos, van muy cortos de escribas. El salario básico es muy bajo, claro, pero con todas esas horas extra puedes ganar mucho dinero. Eso sí, yo no se lo diría a los enanos: son propensos a colgar a cualquiera que tenga relación con los impuestos.

The Altdorf Stage.name: La etapa de Altdorf
The Altdorf Stage.text:
Cargados como van con una caja grande y pesada y una fecha de entrega que se acerca con rapidez, deben encontrar un transporte para ir a Middenheim. La opción más obvia es ir en diligencia, pues la caja cabe en el techo con el resto del equipaje –con un poco de trabajo y unos cuantos chelines para los cocheros–, pero no es la única opción.

Los PJs pueden alquilar, o incluso comprar, un carro. Si bien esto les ahorra el precio de la diligencia, quizá les resulte más difícil pernoctar en las casas de postas del camino. La mayoría tienen acuerdos con las principales compañías de diligencias, que garantizan comida y camas para sus pasajeros, alimento para sus caballos, prioridad para cualquier reparación necesaria y seguridad para el equipaje: es posible que los viajeros que pasan por allí sin avisar se encuentren con que todas estas cosas escasean.

Los caballos son más rápidos que los carromatos y más independientes que las diligencias, pero la caja puede representar un problema. Pesa como un jinete más o menos y es demasiado grande para llevarla en una silla de montar. Un caballo o una mula requieren pasar un Chequeo Normal (+0) de Carisma animal para aceptar esa inusual carga, que se caerá de fallarse el Chequeo. Asegúrate de describir el siniestro golpe que produce la caja y su contenido cuando caen al suelo.

Se pueden encontrar reglas más detalladas para diligencias, carros y animales de carga en el Compendio de El Enemigo en las Sombras.

El resto de este capítulo supone que los Personajes van en diligencia. Si no es el caso, haz los ajustes que consideres necesarios.

Las compañías de diligencias

Un viajero que quiera ir de esta forma de Altdorf a Middenheim puede elegir entre tres compañías de diligencias: @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.XGUpnYfS67guNIWJ.JournalEntryPage.R2BCxi4CJH4hUrru#four-seasons-coaches]{Cuatro Estaciones}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.MomqBNXC7pOwzeue]{Roca del Castillo}, y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.XGUpnYfS67guNIWJ.JournalEntryPage.R2BCxi4CJH4hUrru#ratchett-lines]{Líneas Ratchett}.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.XGUpnYfS67guNIWJ.JournalEntryPage.R2BCxi4CJH4hUrru#four-seasons-coaches]{Cuatro Estaciones} se está expandiendo rápidamente, y sus diligencias salen a diario de Altdorf con destino a todo el Imperio. Como parte de esta expansión, la compañía está adquiriendo posadas a lo largo de todos los caminos principales para uso exclusivo de sus pasajeros. Cada día y durante todo el año, a las diez de la mañana sale una diligencia desde la capital hasta Middenheim.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.MomqBNXC7pOwzeue]{La compañía Roca de Castillo} tiene su sede en Middenheim y pelea duro para mantener su cuota de la ruta de la capital. Ha cerrado acuerdos con muchas posadas independientes a lo largo de ésta y ha frustrado los esfuerzos de Cuatro Estaciones para hacerse con varias posadas entre Altdorf y Middenheim. Las diligencias salen hacia la Ciudad del Lobo Blanco cada dos días (wellentag, marktag, mezahltag y angestag) a las siete de la mañana.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.XGUpnYfS67guNIWJ.JournalEntryPage.R2BCxi4CJH4hUrru#ratchett-lines]{Líneas Ratchett} es una empresa más pequeña, emplazada en Altdorf, como Cuatro Estaciones, aunque es más antigua. Algunos nobles prefieren a esta compañía por su historia y porque sus familias siempre han utilizado los servicios de ésta. Bajo la creciente presión de Cuatro Estaciones, las diligencias de su flota parecen anticuadas y un poco cutres, pero sus empleados se enorgullecen de la calidad del servicio que prestan. 

Líneas Ratchett intenta hacerse un hueco como transportista exclusivo y de clase alta, cobrando un 10% más que sus competidores. Las diligencias de esta compañía no siguen un horario regular: las que contratan los pasajeros nobles salen lo antes posible, con independencia de la hora, mientras que las otras salen cuando todos los asientos están ocupados.

Compañeros de viaje

Aunque el grupo podría reservar una diligencia para ellos solos, quizá sea más entretenido introducir algunos compañeros de viaje interesantes. El número de posibles acompañantes depende del tamaño del grupo y del sitio que haya en la diligencia: la mayoría tienen capacidad para un máximo de seis pasajeros en el interior y otros seis en el portaequipajes.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.Pa77IT9maJR1nU7M]{Alex Eisen}

Por mucho que los aventureros hayan intentado evitarlo, el insufrible barquero siempre puede reaparecer: tal vez su transporte estaba lleno, o lo han echado por ofender a otro pasajero de mayor categoría o entre los demás pasajeros había no humanos o extranjeros o personas de uno de los muchos grupos que le desagradan.

‘¡El mundo es un pañuelo!’ exclama una voz familiar cuando los PJs suben a la diligencia. ‘Y yo que me temía que el viaje iba a ser aburrido. Un pequeño cambio de planes, como veis, pero todo ha salido bien. Nunca terminé de hablaros de esos elfos, ¿verdad? Planean apoderarse de los ríos, así como del océano’.

La cara de los PJs lo dice todo. Va a ser un viaje muy largo y pesado, sobre todo si las estentóreas opiniones de Alex llevan a conflictos en alguna posada en el camino. Si ven al grupo viajando con él, también podrían expulsarlos a ellos.

Las hermanas Jung

Ulrike y Bertha Jung, las hijas de un próspero lanero de Altdorf, viajan a Middenheim para visitar a su hermana @UUID[Actor.431EWVoIAsdZFHPU]{Kirsten Jung}, una dama de la corte. Las acompaña su guardaespaldas, Gunder.

Ambas mujeres son jóvenes (19 y 17 años respectivamente) y bastante refinadas, a todas luces. Si se precisan valores de juego, son a la vez @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.wczCPcuHT4VQDLpL.JournalEntryPage.h7GdfctKdjWL0Ejp]{Comerciantes} y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.wczCPcuHT4VQDLpL.JournalEntryPage.XHYgf5oEwIeCEVNM]{Oficinistas}, con Habilidades, como Carisma, Etiqueta (gremio) y Cotilleo; así como Talentos como @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.8lSoPDGrmeTIaapm]{Gregario}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.GogGbYxkVdCmiKqf]{Leer/Escribir}, y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.LPgjE0cexTVOBVCY]{Cortés}.

Calaveras de la muerte voladoras

Algunos jugadores grognards reconocerán a estas dos damas y a su guardaespaldas de la aventura Grapes of Wrath (NdC: Las Uvas de la Ira, en España apareció en la recopilación Tumbas Saqueadas de Edge para la 2ª. Edición), que se publicó por primera vez en el número 98 de la revista White Dwarf (febrero 1988) y se reimprimió en 1989 en The Restless Dead (NdC: No llegó a traducirse aunque La Factoría usó el nombre provisional de Descanse Sin Paz). Si es así, seguro que esperan que la diligencia se vea atacada por calaveras voladoras.

En este libro, eso no ocurre, pero dichas calaveras aparecen en el @UUID[JournalEntry.aNYMrBowuSB7g7wd]{Compendio de El Poder tras el Trono}.

Gunder es enorme, pero no brillante que digamos. Tiene una frente gruesa e inclinada y una enorme mandíbula que parece sobresalir más que su nariz retorcida y achatada. Va vestido con una chaqueta de cuero y armado con una enorme hacha. Es un @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.wczCPcuHT4VQDLpL.JournalEntryPage.HndWncfaHb0nzNUq]{Guardia} y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.wczCPcuHT4VQDLpL.JournalEntryPage.1OTZ386bMWJ6wfzX]{Soldado} retirado, con Talentos como Amenazador y Rasgos como @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.GbDyBCu8ZjDp6dkj]{beligerante} y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.a8MC97PLzl10WocT]{grande}. Sólo tiene Inteligencia 22, pero dados su fuerza y su carácter imponente, ello nunca le ha supuesto un problema.

Las damiselas estarán encantadas de entablar una conversación educada durante el viaje, pero pobre del PJ que no les muestre el debido respeto. Si los aventureros les han causado una buena impresión antes de llegar a Middenheim, quizá les presenten a su hermana Kirsten. Se alojan en las habitaciones del palacio exterior durante su estancia en la ciudad.

Los peregrinos

@UUID[.j6in1dABcK35SnPQ]{El Lugar de la Roca brillante} es un santuario que hay cerca de Kutenholz y que es sagrado tanto para los seguidores de Ulric como de Sigmar. Uno o dos peregrinos (devotos seguidores de uno u otro dios, pero no necesariamente siguiendo una carrera religiosa) se suben en Altdorf y se bajan cerca de Kutenholz, donde un ramal del camino lleva al santuario. Estos compañeros de viaje pueden ser una buena fuente de información sobre la situación religiosa; con una ligera inclinación a favor de su propia fe, por supuesto. Esta información se encuentra en el apartado ‘Noticias y rumores’ en @UUID[.5KNnpHmwPu4zJUdO]{este libro} y en @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.49qp95QA3aWDRmWS.JournalEntryPage.5KxxSWNDw2D0yyFS#news-and-rumours]{Muerte en el Reik}. Es una oportunidad para dar a los jugadores cualquier información que hayan pasado por alto.

El mercenario

Un oficial, retirado hace poco del servicio militar, se dirige a Middenheim con la intención de disfrutar del carnaval antes de alistarse en la Blitztruppe de Baumann, una famosa ‘compañía libre’ o unidad mercenaria que se está reuniendo allí para dirigirse al este en alguna misión confidencial. Aunque no sabe nada de ésta, es capaz de informar a los PJs sobre el conflicto creciente entre @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives1.journals.S1ONBYW4uxw9POV8.JournalEntryPage.560B5HOv7H4S976Z]{Ostland} y @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives1.journals.S1ONBYW4uxw9POV8.JournalEntryPage.dfQbFTT52E2TBIh9]{Talabecland}, que amenaza con desestabilizar una parte importante del Imperio. Al igual que los peregrinos, este soldado puede transmitir noticias y rumores que podrían haberse perdido.

El cartógrafo imperial

Un joven o una joven (Bart o Bella Kurz), vestido con ropa respetable pero descolorida y algo desgastada, se sube en Altdorf después de supervisar cómo cargan en el portaequipajes y aseguran con cuerdas varias maletas y estuches de cuero y madera de forma extraña. Es un cartógrafo que trabaja para el Servicio Imperial de Mediciones, al que han enviado a Middenheim para consultar con miembros del servicio cartográfico de la ciudad sobre la ubicación de varios asentamientos de los cuales todavía no se sabe su posición exacta.

Si los PJs no han oído aún los rumores del cartógrafo del ducado (Gulhein Tobwurst, al que han despedido hace poco por una serie de errores garrafales), Kurz estará encantado de contarles la historia con un tono serio y grave. Se dice que los mapas de Tobwurst muestran la ciudad de Delberz en tantos lugares diferentes que han enviado a emisarios desde Altdorf y Middenheim para buscarla. Se considera a Tobwurst responsable de los ingresos fiscales por impuestos que no se han recaudado en ese oscuro asentamiento.

Una misión piadosa

Una sacerdotisa o monja de Shallya viaja desde Altdorf para ocupar un puesto en el famoso @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives2.journals.NdCkjAamdihWdQqA]{Gran Hospicio}, un hospital aislado que hay cerca de Frederheim, donde se tratan los trastornos de la mente. Se puede encontrar más información sobre este lugar en el Companion de El Poder Tras el Trono. Si alguien a bordo de la diligencia resulta herido entre Altdorf y Frederheim, ella lo atenderá. Por lo demás, se bajará en el pueblecito, donde una monja de Shallya irá a buscarla en una pequeña calesa.

Detalles del Gran Hospicio se pueden encontrar en Los Archivos del Imperio: Volumen II.

Golthog, Ogre Mercenary.name: Golthog, Ogre Mercenary
Golthog, Ogre Mercenary.text:
@UUID[Actor.HJzyyHH1SppX4SkF]{Golthog}was featured in the original edition of Power Behind the Throne as a fellow guest in the @UUID[JournalEntry.OYXb3CKZ79qBHCHK.JournalEntryPage.SGpfZKBFbzFQNeAz#the-templars-arms]{Templar’s Arms} inn. The Ogre could help out in an unexpected Skaven attack (@UUID[JournalEntry.yXOEsyeWgRgbeVmc.JournalEntryPage.QBR9vcY928EotGA2]{Chaos Strikes By Night}) and possibly become a replacement Character. Here is a Fourth Edition version of Golthog. He could be encountered in the @UUID[JournalEntry.OYXb3CKZ79qBHCHK.JournalEntryPage.SGpfZKBFbzFQNeAz#the-templars-arms]{Templar’s Arms} or elsewhere in the city. 

While he is in Middenheim looking for the famous Baumann’s Blitztruppen mercenary band, he might pass the time by entering the @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.i6WOWs7GHFowLc2n#the-minotaur-fights-(wellentag,-aubentag,-marktag,-4–5:00-p.m.)]{Minotaur fights}, seeing a @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.i6WOWs7GHFowLc2n#middenball-(backertag-and-bezahltag-3–8:00-p.m.,-konigstag-2–7:0]{Snotball match}, catching the @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.KpqRowmWBtz2W6GI#barnumbles-incredible-elephant-show-(marktag-backertag,-5–7:00-p]{elephant show} (he likes elephants — they’re nice and big), or even @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.KpqRowmWBtz2W6GI#challenges-to-the-graf-s-champion-(wellentag-backertag,-11-a.m.–]{challenging the Graf ’s champion}. All these events are described in @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.AFepPfcG3XjWyshD]{The Carnival}. Alternatively, he might have been hired as extra muscle by anyone whom the Characters have made threats against or been investigating too closely.

Baumann’s Blitztruppen

The Characters will have heard rumours about Baumann’s Blitztruppen as they made their way toward Middenheim, and more will be heard about them in future adventures. However, if Golthog becomes a Character, he will have to give up his intention of joining them — they are about to leave for a mission in the east of the Empire, and that is not compatible with the next stage in the campaign.

A Player Character Golthog, and other Characters if necessary, should be gently discouraged from joining the Blitztruppen, or at least persuaded to delay their enlistment until after the carnival. By that time, events will have taken a turn, and the Characters will have far more serious matters to occupy them than joining a mercenary company!

Cameo Adventures.name: Cameo Adventures
Cameo Adventures.text: In this chapter, you will find a selection of short adventures and encounters that can be used in various ways. They can be dropped into Power Behind the Throne as distractions, to slow the Characters down if they are making too much progress too quickly, or they can be used as separate adventures and encounters in Middenheim. With a little adaptation, most of them could be set in any of the Empire’s great cities or larger towns.

Devouring the World.name: Devouring the World
Devouring the World.text:
By now the Characters may have become accustomed to the facing off against cultists of the Ruinous Powers. While always terrifying, the may feel that they have come to understand their enemy. However, there are others powers at work in the world, and one in particular has plagued Middenheim since its very founding.

Of all the enemies that faced Middenheim throughout the ages, the first, and perhaps the greatest, was @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.actors.AGyoIt9stdSin46x]{Babrakkos the Liche-Thing}. The undying creature is so integral to the legends surrounding Middenheim’s early days that it is sometimes known as the First Threat. A vile undead monstrosity, Babrakkos remains a puzzle to the scholars of the Collegium Theologica, for it bears little resemblance to Vampires or the revenant kings of distant Khemri. Yet its connection to such things is undeniable. Babrakkos cheated death and commanded animated corpses as its soldiers and servants.

While Babrakkos could be said to have been killed, there is no place in Morr’s realm for such a foul abomination. Its spirit still lingers around Middenheim in anticipation of the day it will return to lay waste to the heirs of the heroes who once slew it.

A group called @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.aDZDPaz2G4yzBedC]{The Eaters of the World} has grown up around the worship of Babrakkos. They seek to usher in their master’s return, and have long been hunted in Middenheim. In the present day their influence is reduced but not gone. They prefer to work through subtle means, spreading crescent shaped icons of the creature across the city. This has the effect of slowly increasing their master’s presence. In a nameless cellar the cultists gather to give praise, and in an unmarked throne a half scene figure slowly grows more substantial. Babrakkos will return once more, and Middenheim will burn.

Unbidden Gifts 

While the Characters are enjoying the events of the carnival, they are approached by one Eric Schmidt, a young man dressed in carnival attire who is freely handing out small amulets. They are small crescent moons cheaply made and tied to a simple hemp twine. He pushes one to the hands of at least one Character, and bids them to wear it. 

If asked about the meaning of the amulet, Eric will shrug and say they are from a tradition as old as Middenheim, and represent rebirth. He will then continue down the street handing out the amulets to random passers by.

If the Characters choose to wear the amulet, they will notice little effect during the first day. However, for each additional day they wear it, make an Average (+20) Cool Test on behalf of the Character. If they fail, they are troubled by bad dreams of a shadowy figure just out of sight, resting on an unadored throne. If they suffer an Impressive Failure or worse, they also gain one @Condition[Fatigued] Condition which lasts for the rest of the day.

In Middenheim, the prevalence of Ghur makes it hard to pick up on subtle magical details, so any investigation of the amulet by a Character with Magic Sight will reveal little if undertaken inside the city. However, if the amulet is studied outside of Middenheim a subtle note of Shyish can be detected. 

If the Characters look for Eric Schmidt, he can be found around the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.0cqPwan7hGfgWhJH]{Great Park} during the @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.Q6j1wVRrCC2DhUDo#the-festival-of-fine-ales-(wellentag,-aubentag,-marktag,-noon-to]{Festival of Fine Ales}, and later outside the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.QmdIq7fCxqTn5a5K]{Royal Opera House}, still handing out his amulets. If confronted he will plead ignorance, but offer to take the amulet back. He will continue to plead innocent until a chance to escape presents itself, at which point he will hiss ‘May his hunger find you last of all,’ before sprinting off. If killed, they will see a look of calm cross Schmidts face as he dies, before his eyes roll back in his head and he screams ‘Babrakkos! My soul to feed yours!"

If the Characters pursue this further, they find themselves the target of yet another cult with agents at every level of Middenheim society. Details for weaving a larger adventure around the return of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.actors.AGyoIt9stdSin46x]{Babrakkos} can be found in Middenheim: City of the White Wolf.

The Wine of Madness.name: The Wine of Madness
The Wine of Madness.text:
This short adventure can be used to add another layer of complication to the end of the Carnival in Power Behind the Throne, and strengthen the role of @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard Wallenstein} in the adventure. If the Players already have their hands full, it may be omitted or used at another time in another city. Before running this adventure, it is advisable to read @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba]{The Jade Sceptre: A GM’s Guide}.

The Jade Sceptre in Middenheim

The followers of Slaanesh in Middenheim have seen more auspicious times: like other Chaos cults in the city, they have suffered from the rise of the Purple Hand. However, the cult of the Jade Sceptre is active enough, and the schemes of one member in particular should provide the Characters with plenty to think about.

The most active cell revolves around a small group of wealthy young rakes who style themselves ‘The Deviants and Decadents’ .This inner circle has a surprising amount of political influence, if it should choose to use it, although not as much as the Purple Hand can bring to bear. Still, the Jade Sceptre could become a significant power in the city if its members looked up from their excessive indulgence long enough to formulate a plan. So far, they have not. Recently, a more ambitious member has joined their ranks.

Gotthard von Wittgenstein

@UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard von Wittgenstein} is the last remaining member of an ancient but little-known Reikland family. The von Wittgensteins had risen to prominence in the service of the Empress Margaritha in the 1980s (Imperial Calendar), but since then they have sunk back into obscurity. For one reason or another (but mainly because each succeeding generation was developing more and more mutations), none of the family had left their barony for more than seventy years.

Gotthard was bored in the family's crumbling castle, tired of the same old faces (and beaks, and tentacles): his sister spent all her time hunched over dismembered corpses; his brother was obsessed with taxidermy; his mother was completely deranged; and his father looked more like a giant cockroach every day. Eventually, he could bear it no longer.

Although, rather surprisingly, they had yet to receive a call from the Witch Hunters, the von Wittgensteins had developed a rather unsavoury reputation among the riverfolk who passed beneath their towering castle. Mutants seemed more numerous in those waters, to say nothing of corpses. He had developed a correspondence with a friend in Middenheim, who hinted at dark pleasures that he knew he would have to experience for himself.

@UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard von Wittgenstein} arrived in the city a few months ago, and through the influence of high-ranking cult members and his own boundless energy and ambition, he rose quickly. Under the assumed name of Gotthard Wallenstein, he became not only the Chairman of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild} but also the Convenor of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.rCpAPw22cl9dsEnl]{Komission for Commerce, Trade, and Taxation}, giving him considerable power over the city’s economy. So far, he has only used this power to line his own pockets and those of his friends, but he has something special planned for the last night of the Carnival.

Gotthard’s Plan

As readers will gather from Power Behind the Throne, Carnival week is a raucous time, when the normally dour Middenheimers let loose and enjoy themselves. People come from all over the Empire to join in the festivities: it is a time of spectacular parties, and monumental hangovers. This year, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild} has announced that on the last night of the Carnival, it will pay for every fountain in the city to flow with wine instead of water. Although Gotthard believes the idea was his alone, it was in fact subtly suggested to him by the Law Lord (and Purple Hand leader) @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Karl-Heinz Wasmeier}, who thought it a good way to blunt public outrage at the new taxes he is forcing through, while simultaneously focusing attention on the merchants rather than the Law Lords. Such a display of conspicuous wealth, coupled with a few well-placed rumours, will promote the idea that the merchants are somehow behind the new measures, or at least that they are profiting handsomely from them.

Unknown to Wasmeier, @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard}— who is completely ignorant of Wasmeier’s plot or his status as a member of the Purple Hand — has added a further detail to the plan. He has obtained a huge quantity of a drug known as @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.items.VWTPVAGlcFf48qCX]{Estalian Mosca}, a powerful stimulant rumoured to fuel many wild parties, and plans to spike the free wine with it. For the last night of the Carnival and most of the following day, Middenheim will become one vast revelry, a tribute that will surely attract the notice of Slaanesh and may even lead to the city’s fall.

Preparations

Through cult contacts in Marienburg, @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard} has obtained three barrels of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.items.VWTPVAGlcFf48qCX]{Mosca}: a huge quantity, representing tens of thousands of individual doses. Brought into the city under the cover of the hundreds of barrels supplying the @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.Q6j1wVRrCC2DhUDo#the-festival-of-fine-ales-(wellentag,-aubentag,-marktag,-noon-to]{Festival of Fine Ales} at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.0cqPwan7hGfgWhJH]{Great Park}, Gotthard inspects the barrels when he visits on Wellentag around 1 p.m. Having marked the barrels in question, he goes about his business while one of his trusted agents, a dissolute lass named Addic, will ‘buy’ the ‘ales’ in question and have them delivered to a restaurant and tavern in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.t1wYBKV4LW8o0XJ1]{Neumarkt}-@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.pvuBkAdDt7cuaIud]{Osttor} district called the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dqgQgjdmiCrfJAzx]{Templar’s Downfall}, ostensibly to add to their stock. From there, the schemers decant the drug into empty wine bottles, which are ‘delivered’ in cases of twelve bottles to various warehouses around the city, where the wine purchased by the Guild is stored. It takes several days for the cult to spike all of the wine, but everything should be complete in time for the promised filling of the fountains on Festag evening.

The Best-Laid Plans

As simple as this plan is, there are a number of things that can go wrong, tipping off the Characters that something sinister is afoot and prompting them to investigate. Here is one example.

A Simple Mistake

If they are at the @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.Q6j1wVRrCC2DhUDo#the-festival-of-fine-ales-(wellentag,-aubentag,-marktag,-noon-to]{Festival of Fine Ales} between noon and 1 p.m., the Characters come upon a commotion at a beer tent with a sign outside reading ‘J. Thijksson, Marienburg’. If the Characters investigate, they see several employees and bystanders struggling to hold steady a clearly intoxicated Carnival-goer spewing an increasingly incomprehensible stream of colourful lanauge. The drunkard is raving in the language filthy enough to make a state soldier blush, and when brought outside the tent turns his vitriol first towards a series of horrified patrons who seem to know him, then to a nearby tent pole, a rain barrel — anything within earshot.

A successful Challenging (+0) Perception Test (+10 for Physicians, Spies, or anyone else who has practical knowledge of drugs and poisons) reveals a strange, glazed look in the drunkard’s eyes, a flush in his face, and profuse sweat running down his forehead and cheeks, quite out of keeping with the weather. Others may make an Easy (+40) Intelligence Test to observe that it is very early in the day for anyone, even a seasoned drinker, to be as drunk as this man seems to be. At that exact moment, his eyes start almost out of his head, his whole body is wracked by a tremendous spasm, and he falls down dead with blood leaking out of his eyes, ears, and mouth.

Questioning the staff and bystanders turns up that the man came into the tent with his fiancée and a number of friends and relations from both families. He ordered a beer, took one sip, and spat it out with an oath, saying that it was not beer at all. The embarrassed tent staff took the barrel off and were in the process of tapping another one when the drinker apparently went insane.

If the Characters try to locate the barrel, they are pointed to one at the side of the tent that turns out to be empty, and seems perfectly normal. An observant bystander may be able to tell them that the drinker was served from a barrel marked only with a plain looking label, but the empty barrel bears a familiar brewers seal, as do all the others that the Characters can see.

The unfortunate drinker was accidentally served a full tankard of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.items.VWTPVAGlcFf48qCX]{Mosca} by a staff member who is not in on the plot, and one swig was enough to cause a fatal overdose. One of the tent’s staff, an intermediary for the @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba.JournalEntryPage.t8P7AnjdFtYJfkgM]{Jade Sceptre}, hurried it out of sight in the curtained stock area at the back of the tent before the Characters arrived, which is where it should have been all along. The three barrels of Mosca are hidden among almost a hundred others, stacked at the back of the tent to serve the day’s drinkers, and the Characters are not permitted to interfere with the stock: the staff call the Watch if they persist in investigating the inventory.

No matter how they try, the Characters are unable to find anything wrong with the beer sold in the tent. If they try to claim that the tent’s beer is poisoned, they are thrown out; any complaints to the Watch are met with polite skepticism and a promise to investigate ‘in due course’. This, naturally, never happens.

If the Characters are still at the tent at 1 p.m., they see Gotthard arrive, although they may not know who he is. He seems to be just another well-to-do festival-goer until, mug in hand, he motions one of the staff to one side. A Hard (–20) Lore (Chaos) Test or a Difficult (–10) Lore (Slaanesh) Test leads a Character to recognise a Jade Sceptre hand sign in the exchange of gestures. After a whispered exchange, he goes through into the stock area, emerging about thirty seconds later, finishing his drink, and carrying on with a circuit of the festival. Along the way, the Characters may be able to see him nod to a disreputable-looking woman — Addic — in passing.

If they watch the tent, Addic arrives an hour or so later with a donkey-cart and three hired guards, loading up the three barrels and driving to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dqgQgjdmiCrfJAzx]{Templar’s Downfall}. The Characters have a chance to intercept the cart at this point, although the Watch will not look favourably on anything that seems like attempted robbery, especially if the guards — a sensible precaution for anyone moving drink across the city during Carnival week — are injured.

Once in the Templar’s Downfall, the barrels are safe from anything less than a full-scale assault. Secure in the cellar, the drug is decanted. If they are still watching the place at noon the following day, the Characters see several crates of bottled wine being loaded on to a cart for delivery to the Merchants’ Guild, but they will not see any barrels leaving and they will not know that anything is wrong with the ‘wine’.

If the Characters manage to sneak or force their way into the cellar of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dqgQgjdmiCrfJAzx]{Templar’s Downfall} before the process is complete, they find it crowded with @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba.JournalEntryPage.VUkVgTsnVJIAznf0]{Jade Sceptre cultists} who attack any intruders on sight. They outnumber the Characters by at least three to one, and are desperate to ensure that no word of their activities gets out. If the Characters manage to get into the cellar after noon on Aubentag, they find the three marked barrels, all empty. It takes a Hard (–20) Extended Trade (Apothecary) or Trade (Poisoner) Test with 8 required SLs to identify the rapidly drying residue inside the barrels as @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.items.VWTPVAGlcFf48qCX]{Estalian Mosca}, with each roll requiring about five minutes of examination.

What Now?

Even if the Characters have realised what is going on, and have followed the trail from the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dqgQgjdmiCrfJAzx]{Templar’s Downfall} to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild}, they will not simply be able to storm in and expose the plot. The Guild, and @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard} as its Chairman and Convenor of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.rCpAPw22cl9dsEnl]{Komission on Commerce, Trade, and Taxation}, have too much clout for a wild accusation from a group of adventurers from out of town to be taken seriously.

If they decide to take action themselves, they will have to track down all the tainted wine before it reaches fountains all across the city, and either take it or destroy it. Neither course is likely to endear them to the thousands of people who are looking forward to free wine, and the results could range from a mob beating to a full-blown riot.

Oh, What A Night

The rest of this adventure is left to the GM, based on the Characters’ actions so far, the contacts they have made within the city, and how they decide to deal with the problem. At the GM’s option, the city may indeed see a night of unbridled havoc if they fail, perhaps accompanied by @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.8gG2Wim6wAlJWRax]{Daemonettes} appearing here and there.

The Daemon Drink

Alternatively, some other power may step in and save the day. For example, a faction of hard-line temperance campaigners (possibly led by one or more flagellants) might lay siege to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dqgQgjdmiCrfJAzx]{Templar’s Downfall}, denouncing it as a den of iniquity and making it impossible to move the tainted barrels to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.xBB5HI6Ojii4cW2s]{Merchants’ Guild}. They might gather outside the guild house, making it impossible to take the wine to the fountains, or they might attack the fountains themselves.

Sigmarite flagellants, of course, might cause a riot simply by their presence in the city, so perhaps the protests are led by a priest of Ulric — possibly a @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.nzsWxG9db2fdGjZM.JournalEntryPage.0sKLAqTMd6KMG9zw]{Wolf-Kin} — who was granted a vision warning of a threat to the city from the wine. 

In any event, the protest devolves into a series of riots as townsfolk and visitors exchange harsh words, improvised missiles, and blows with the protestors. The situation continues to spiral out of control until the Watch has to intervene in force, which might prevent them from being somewhere else at a crucial time.

For an added layer of complication, the protestors might include some followers of Khorne from a local cult (such as the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.5wnsKJZg364dFeg1#the-crimson-skull]{Crimson Skull} — for the Blood God and the Prince of Pleasure are implacable enemies). The two cults will fight it out under cover of the riots.

In Vino Verminous

To add to the confusion even further, the Skaven might steal the tainted wine to help in their attack on the city at the end of which will occur during The Horned Rat. Bottles or cases of the wine are planted in the kitchens of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.PJSTe8IXwh6oy78t]{Collegium Theologica}, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.m0gDOo9sztuTymsb]{Wizards’ and Alchemists’ Guilds}, and other selected locations, to lower their defences and make it easier for the assorted and sometimes conflicting Skaven plans to come to fruition.

Ending the Adventure

The adventure ends when the plot has been thwarted, or when the fountains begin to flow with the tainted wine. The Characters may have learned more about the cult of the @UUID[JournalEntry.gX4TCKy0TPwS68ba.JournalEntryPage.t8P7AnjdFtYJfkgM]{Jade Sceptre} and @UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard von Wittgenstein}, and they may know that he is the last of the von Wittgensteins, living under an assumed name. They may have earned themselves some leverage with a major figure in the city, just in time to make use of it in the plot of Power Behind the Throne. Although Gotthard’s influence is limited, every little helps!

If things have not gone well, the Characters will not only have failed to stop the attack on the city, but wasted precious time. They will have some catching up to do if they want to thwart the greater plot of Karl-Heinz Wasmeier and the Purple Hand.

For total success in this adventure — the plot foiled and Gotthard exposed or turned into a tool for the Characters to use — each Character should be awarded @Exp[100,Foiled or exposed Gotthard's Plan]{100 Experience Points}, with the usual bonuses for bright ideas and good roleplaying. For partial success or failure, reduce the awards in proportion to the party’s achievements.

Nice Teddy....name: Nice Teddy...
Nice Teddy....text:
This incident takes place during the day, while the Characters are wandering through any area where they are likely to encounter an entertainer — @UUID[JournalEntry.HxC5snuKA2z7PACe.JournalEntryPage.vIJ90tQ4538VwSgA]{Initial Inquiries} gives more information on this. An entertainer stands on a street corner playing on her flute while a dancing bear shuffles comically to the music. It wears an iron collar attached to a chain looped through the piper's belt.

A small crowd has gathered, including a number of street urchins who jeer and play dares to see who will go closest to the animal. One of them throws a stone, hitting the bear in the eye. With a bellow of pain, it lunges forward, snapping the chain taut and pulling the piper off her feet. The crowd scatters as it advances on the stone-thrower, dragging the struggling piper behind it.

By the time the Characters are able to do anything, the bear has trapped the urchin in a corner, and the piper is still unsuccessfully struggling to regain her feet. She is shouting to the bear to stay still, but without effect.

The bear has a @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.KtYgLHcSLpHmnGI2]{standard profile} but its Movement score is reduced to 3 due to dragging the piper. Characters with a higher Initiative score than the bear must still make a successful Initiative Test in order to act before it can attack the cornered urchin. You should also make a Challenging (+0) Initiative Test for the piper at the beginning of each Round, based on a score of 31. On the first successful Test, she regains her feet and starts using her Animal Training Skill (45) to calm the bear, provided it is not in combat. If any Character attacks the bear, it cannot be calmed down unless it is first successfully distracted (see below). 

The Characters have a number of options apart from simply standing by and watching the terrified urchin be shredded.

Attacking

The Characters can attack the bear and try to kill it — this is probably the least satisfactory option. Although it saves the urchin and perhaps many others, the piper is not happy about losing her livelihood!

Distraction

Secondly, they can try to distract the bear long enough for the urchin to escape. If the Characters try this, make a Challenging (+0) Willpower Test for the bear. If it fails, it is distracted long enough to allow the urchin to escape. However, it is still angry, and attacks the nearest Character unless it can be calmed with a Charm Animal Test opposed by the bear’s Willpower. A single SL on the Opposed Test is enough to calm the bear long enough for the piper to regain her senses and pacify her friend.

The Chain

The Characters can take hold of the bear’s chain and try to pull it away. Only Characters who make a successful Challenging (+0) Cool Test can summon the courage to do this, but the Test may be attempted once per Round until successful. Make an Opposed Test using the total Strength scores of the Characters pulling on the chain, and the bear’s Strength of 55, repeating each Round until successful. This draws the bear’s attention, allowing the piper to calm it.

Charm

A Character can calm the bear down on a successful Average (+20) Charm Animal Test. If the Characters fail the Test, the attempt counts as a distraction (see above).

Magic

A spellcaster might try to save the day with magic. While the bear is too large to be affected by the Petty spell @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.gQ14yfwjfcJgNpMp]{Animal Friend}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.4ePe5oNQakA8nJlk]{Sleep} might be useful, as might @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.WeIdAA7KArjUZfyH]{Entangle} or the Lore of Beasts spells @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.FaHVRxdljzqklNTC]{Beast Master} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.gwnNz34Rh0jW4WmF]{Beast Tongue}. Resourceful Players will be able to come up with many more ideas.

The best spells to use are those that can calm, subdue, or entangle the bear quickly. Wounding spells might be effective, but most enrage the bear further, forcing the Characters to kill the bear. The Characters receive no thanks from the piper who has just lost her star attraction. Spells and miracles with an area of effect risk wounding the urchin as well as the bear, and possibly the nearer bystanders.

Resolution

The entertainer might make for an interesting contact if she is happy with the Characters’ resolution. She has regular dealings with the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.Liw9HcyJnHbLZevz.JournalEntryPage.xiXbVzAggcmfXxd1]{Low Kings’} thugs and dealmakers and has heard whispers of Chaos cults operating within Middenheim. The extent of her knowledge is up to the GM, but she freely shares it for the Characters’ help.

If the Characters kill the bear, the urchin runs off at the first opportunity, and any attempt to prevent this is met with a kick in the shins. The urchin escapes automatically, and the kicked character must make a successful Challenging (+0) Willpower Test or spend one Round hopping and cursing.

Each Character who participates in any action that leads to the urchin getting away should receive @Exp[30,Helped the urchin get away]{30 Experience Points}. This award is halved if the bear is killed, and at the GM’s option Taal may decide that the Character is due some Sin points. Characters who manage to subdue the bear without harming it receive @Exp[50, Subdued the Bear with no harm]{50 Experience}.

Watch The Birdie....name: Watch The Birdie...
Watch The Birdie....text:
This incident could be used almost anywhere in the city, but is perhaps most effective either in a market area or wherever large numbers of moderately wealthy people are likely to be walking about. The incident takes place in daylight.

About 30 yards away, there is a sudden blur of action. There is a scream and some shouting, and a bird flies away rapidly, with people throwing stones and other improvised missiles at it. Any Character with an appropriate Skill can identify the bird as a magpie. What do the Characters do?

Rushing to Help

If the Characters hurry to the scene of the activity, they find a distraught, middle-aged woman from whom the bird has just stolen a jewelled hair-pin, or a furious stallholder from whom it has stolen some small but valuable trinket, or some other victim from whom the bird has stolen something small, shiny, and valuable. By the time they reach the scene, the bird is long gone. If the Characters have failed to make the acquaintance of a major NPC, this could be an opportunity to introduce them — the woman above could be one of the Ladies of the Court, for example.

Shooting

The Characters suffer from the usual –20 penalty for shooting at a Little target. There is time for one round of missile fire from the moment the Characters first see the bird to when it disappears behind a tree or rooftop. The bird is flying fast and fairly low, so the Characters’ shots may endanger bystanders and could cause a panic. In this event, a Watch patrol arrives on the scene in [[/r 2d10]] rounds, and the party may be charged with causing a breach of the peace. If the Characters manage to bring the bird down, they are able to explain the situation to the Watch and may get away with a warning and perhaps a spot fine of a Crown or two. Otherwise, a successful Challenging (+0) Charm Test, bribery, or some other means is needed to avoid a heavier penalty: a fine of [[/r 2d10]] GCs and the confiscation of their missile weapons.

If the bird is brought down and the stolen object recovered, the victim offers to pay any fine the Characters may have incurred, and gives them 5 GCs as a reward.

Pursuit

If the Characters decide to follow the bird, you may make use of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.bdfiyhEYtKs7irqc#pursuit]{pursuit rules}, though unless they can themselves fly they will not catch the creature, merely keep up with it. The bird has an effective Agility of 33 and a Move of 8. Talents such as @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.9h82z72XGo9tfgQS]{Excellent Vision} give the usual bonuses. If they manage to keep the bird in sight for 5 successive rounds, they see it fly through a window into the attic of a building several streets away. A successful Challenging (+0) lntelligence or Average (+20) Navigation Test Test is required for the Characters to find the building.

The building stands a storey taller than those around it, and there is a single door at street level. Going through the door, the Characters find a narrow hallway with doors on either side and a staircase leading upwards. The building is split into apartments, and after two or three landings the Characters reach the door to the attic. The door is locked, but fairly flimsy — a Challenging (+0) Strength Test will see it smashed off its hinges.

Beyond the door is a small attic room furnished with a bed, a table with two chairs, and a small cupboard. A small, wiry, shabbily dressed man of about thirty is sitting on the bed, which is strewn with brightly shining baubles of all descriptions. As the Characters enter the room, a raven takes off in alarm from its perch on the back of a chair and flies out of the window. As soon as he sees that he is outnumbered, the thief surrenders, but he attempts to escape if the opportunity arises.

If the Characters turn him over to the authorities, they receive a reward of @Credit[17gc10ss]{17 GCs 10/–}, this being 10% of the value of the goods recovered. On the other hand, this thief could be useful if the Characters wish to make contact with the city’s underworld. In either case, a reward of @Exp[25, Discovered the thief]{25 Experience Points} is appropriate for each character who helps the party discover the operation.

Further Possibilities

The Characters might witness several aerial robberies over a period of time, all in the same general area, until they decide to take action. They could hear rumours of a bird stealing small items of jewellery on a few occasions, or witness a dispute between a stallholder and a shopper who claims that a trinket on the stall was stolen from them a few days ago. The operation can make a good piece of background noise, to distract the players from the main thread of their adventure and to help create the feeling that things are happening in Middenheim even when their Characters aren't around.

Down Among the Dead Men.name: Down Among the Dead Men
Down Among the Dead Men.text:
This encounter takes place in or around Morrspark at night. The Characters spot two figures in the shadows, either coming out of a family crypt or heading away from the Morrspark. They are carrying something that looks remarkably like a body wrapped up in sack-cloth.

Spotted!

If the Characters challenge the grave robbers or otherwise make their presence known, the thieves drop the body and run for it, quickly losing any pursuit in the streets of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.ZL7xqH1Rzd6GtRHr]{Westor}-@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.saNnWrr5EyTyZoxE]{Sudgarten}district and heading back to Ostwald. The Characters can call the Watch, who quickly summon a priest of Morr to the scene. After about half an hour of making statements and tying up formalities, the Characters are rewarded with @Credit[10gc mode=split]{10 GCs} by the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.tPgvZoYSi1URdTeL]{Temple of Morr}: the standing reward for thwarting body-snatchers and Necromancers.

Trailing the Thieves

If the Characters follow the grave robbers, they see them load the body into a small cart hidden on a side-street off the West Weg. The thieves drive off across the city, through a maze of side-streets. They cross @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.QM1S0gchPUOzsjKr]{Ulricsmund}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.Iyfbu0akp7qznUqR]{Geldmund} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.1m2DJYLbVzzIR4Sy]{Altmarkt}before pulling up at a building in the Freiburg, where a third figure waits in the shadows to receive the body.

The Characters can call the Watch at this stage if they wish. A successful Challenging (+0) Bribery or Charm Test is necessary to persuade the Watch to raid the house. If this is successful, the Watch — perhaps with the Characters close behind — discovers the body and catches the miscreants red-handed. The Characters are rewarded with @Credit[10gc mode=split]{10 GCs} as above: this is the standing reward, and is not negotiable.

Instead of calling the Watch, the Characters might decide to stake the house out, or to break in and find out what is going on. If so, the GM has to decide precisely what that is. Some possibilities follow. 

Forbidden Research: The body is being delivered to the house of a Necromancer. The premises are guarded by @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.T79RqnDOAQLn3I1s]{Zombies} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.jfMhkQGzjFWDxVOm]{Cultists}. The Necromancer herself will be alerted by sounds of combat, and will attempt to use magic to kill, and preferably reanimate, the Characters.

In the Name of Science: The body has been delivered to a physician or scholar, who wants it for dissection and research. The house is quiet; servants have been given the night off, and encouraged to visit relatives in other parts of the city, but a few students might be in attendance. The grave robbers lock the body in a laboratory in the basement. Other than the Grave Robbers, the housekeeper has the only key. 

There is an operating table in the laboratory, and shelves around the walls are stacked with limbs and organs in pickling jars. If discovered, the physician or scholar tries to buy the Characters off, starting at @Credit[10gc mode=each]{10 GCs each} and bargaining upwards as the GM sees fit. Even if the Characters accept the bribe, they may still have a later encounter with a band of footpads whom the physician or scholar hires to kill them and recover the money. If the thugs fail, the increasingly paranoid dissectionist may even go so far as to hire an assassin.

A Quick Exit: The ‘body’ is not really dead. Someone — a cultist trying to escape from their cult, a character on the run from a gang, or anything else you care to think of — has staged their own death with the aid of a coma-inducing drug. Shortly after burial, the ‘body’ is recovered by hired grave robbers (who do not know the full story) and delivered to an alchemist or pharmacist, where the antidote is administered. The fugitive is then smuggled out of the city to begin a new life somewhere else. When the Characters break in or the Watch raids the house, they find no body, just a semi-conscious patient receiving treatment. This leaves the Characters with some fast talking to do.

Conclusion

If the Characters bring the incident to a satisfactory conclusion, they should be awarded @Exp[20,Down Among the Dead Men]{20 Experience Points} each, with bonuses as usual for clever ideas and engaging roleplaying.

Experience Awards.name: Experience Awards
Experience Awards.text:
Power Behind the Throne is saturated with chicanery, intrigue, machinations, and skulduggery,  providing ample opportunities for the party as a collective, or the Characters as individuals, to gain many experience points for either preventing or participating in various schemes. The following Experience Points may be awarded at suitable points during the adventure — usually at the end of an evening’s play.  These rewards will also provide some feedback to let them know how they are progressing with the plot. Feel free to award additional Experience Points to Players displaying impressive powers of insight or observation, and other such traits that enhance the enjoyment and experience for everyone at the table. 

Roleplaying

For sessions where roleplaying forms the majority of play, 70–100 points may be awarded. For sessions where roleplaying is mixed with other activities, 30–50 points is appropriate. Truly excellent roleplaying may earn up to a maximum of 70 points per session.

Plot Objectives

Power Behind the Throne stands out for its rich opportunities to gain experience points throughout. Because of this adventure’s unique structure, Experience Point awards are listed by objective rather than by chapter.

The Journey to Middenheim

Note: gaining the support of an NPC involves all the necessary steps. For example, de-hypnotising Dieter, getting an independent supply of Ranald's Delight for Sparsam, and so on. Only Characters who actively participate receive the reward.

@Exp[10,Recovered Reya Ehrlich]{Recovering Reya Ehrlich — 10 points}

@Exp[10,Recovered the blackmail letters]{Recovering the blackmail letters — 10 points}

@Exp[10,Killed/captured ‘Hoflich']{Killing/capturing ‘Hoflich' — 10 points}

For a successful intervention in a plot to overthrow the city, the Characters each receive @Exp[200,Intervened in the plot to overthrow Middenheim]{200 points} and 1 Fate Point. If the party obtained all of Wasmeier’s secret files, they should receive an extra @Exp[100, Obtained Wasmeier's secret files]{100 points} plus another Fate Point.

Josef Sparsam.name: Josef Sparsam
Josef Sparsam.text:
@UUID[Actor.htCpUSEFBVpiknOx]{Josef Sparsam}

Role

In charge of the Middenheim Treasury and all tax officials, Sparsam has moderate influence on Graf Boris (2 votes).

Locations

Sparsam lives in the Palace, and is not easy to approach. Finding a pretext for an appointment requires ingenuity: the Characters could try posing as wealthy merchants or antique dealers.

Reactions

Females: +10 to all Fellowship Tests when Sparsam is under the influence, –10 when not intoxicated. Sparsam is normally timid with anyone he finds attractive.

Academics: Characters whose Intelligence exceeds 40 may use this instead of their Fellowship score adding the advances from any appropriate social skill. Sparsam values intelligence.

Dwarfs: –10 to all Fellowship Tests. Sparsam is apprehensive about their reaction to the tax changes.

Knowledge

Sparsam knows the political system well, but is not a good judge of people. He can be helpful to Characters in matters of protocol, explain how to reach other NPCs, and may provide a crucial pass to the Inner Palace.

Misconceptions

Sparsam believes that @UUID[Actor.2gjtu5TLTG8YCJmh]{Pavarotti} has no influence on Graf Boris. This is only wishful thinking.

Goals

Sparsam’s main goal is to maximise public funds: the tax changes seemed good until he saw the reactions of those affected. He would try to repeal the laws — if he were not being blackmailed (see Deadly Secret: A Powder Problem, below). He collects antiques and enjoys discussing them with other enthusiasts.

The Other Npcs

@UUID[Actor.1UPIDtrSuQv4zUVg]{Dieter Schmiedehammer} — Champion: Indifferent; hardly knows him.

@UUID[Actor.nzNgV71abEH1iNFo]{Rallane Lafarel} — Minstrel: Indifferent; hardly knows him

@UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina Todbringer} — ‘Princess’: When forced to interact with her he is awkward but flattering. He knows that she does not like him. Secretly he thinks she is vacuous and dull.

@UUID[Actor.ZyMHHLG9tNTDIw8S]{Hildegarde Zimperlich} — Chaperone: Fears her malice, and worries that her gossip-mongering might create social traps for him. Their mutual detestation is irrational, but they can hardly conceal it.

@UUID[.ECtQRvrnApRgX7TA]{The Midden Marshals}: No particular personal feelings. The military always want more money, of course, and Sparsam moans about this at length.

@UUID[.BczIUXqbPEOGbY9V]{The Wizards}: Normally has no dealings with them, but recently had to endure the wrath of Deputy High Wizard @UUID[Actor.ZVVaOEUN9ArYrYnM]{Janna Eberhauer} about the Scroll Tax. Having taken a dose of stimulant to fortify himself for the meeting, Sparsam made an ill-judged advance for which the enraged magician threatened to turn him into a rat. He is now terrified of her, and highly apprehensive of High Wizard @UUID[Actor.sN0PeIFSOidPua1f]{Albrecht Helseher}.

@UUID[Actor.VqvKKvGm7y1XzDUe]{High Priest Ar-Ulric}: Dislikes him. He has noticed the High Priest’s agitation, and thinks Ar-Ulric may share his addiction. Sparsam has occasional paranoid fantasies about this sort.

@UUID[Actor.puFBI6fLMjn68Ab2]{Emmanuelle Schlagen} — Paramour: Thinks she is frivolous, and knows she makes sarcastic jokes behind his back. He has been dreaming up a jewellery tax in revenge. Does not know that she is Graf Boris’s paramour, nor is he aware of her affair with Ar-Ulric.

@UUID[.ClmMNlSphPvcNVTy]{Ladies at Court}: Also frivolous. Sparsam resents their allowance from the Treasury (300 Crowns per year, though he will never disclose this). The exception is the icy @UUID[Actor.7ggdqHZxId697kT5]{Natasha Sinnlich}, for whom he is developing a hopeless and somewhat pathetic affection. He made intoxicated advances to @UUID[Actor.RhXJwUjrYOIqcTk4]{Petra Liebkosen} at a recent feast, but remembers nothing of it.

@UUID[Actor.6yFVH9mzC5VoQAUh]{Siegfried Prunkvoll} — Knight Eternal: Knows him slightly through their shared interest in antiques. Thinks he is a fool, but respects him as a symbol of strong, lawful authority. At least he isn’t frivolous.

@UUID[Actor.NBkPZBRIQwPXeLUq]{Allavandrel Fanmaris} — Master of the Hunt: Allavandrel has always been kind to the Chancellor, rescuing him from many painful conversations at the social functions Sparsam dreads. Sparsam is not one to express affection openly, but he is glad that the Elf is around.

@UUID[Actor.54rz079B0PFUaDWp]{Gotthard Wallenstein} — Komission Convenor: Admires him for his tireless and persuasive advocacy of merchants’ interests. They have sherry now and then, and discuss trade. He regards Wallenstein as ‘a stout fellow,’ and knows nothing of his connection with the Chaos Cult of the Jade Sceptre.

@UUID[Actor.2gjtu5TLTG8YCJmh]{Luigi Pavarotti} — Baronial Physician: Embarrassed and disturbed by his impulsive forthrightness, and thinks him ‘a thoroughly bad lot’. However, his mild fear of the man means he will not express his opinion unless certain that Pavarotti will not hear of it.

@UUID[.seoqMOoXusLrB77M]{The Law Lords}: Considers all three to be ‘intelligent chaps’. Works closely with them to plan and draft laws relating to the city’s finances.

@UUID[Actor.f9GN3PQGUp9tjSCT]{Hausmeister Breugal}  — The Chamberlain: Knows Breugal by sight, but has never conversed with him. To Sparsam, Breugal is just a part of the palace furniture.

@UUID[Actor.7meYhAhOFdwPuz6S]{Edel Mueller} - High Priestess: He’s seen her in the company of the @UUID[.seoqMOoXusLrB77M]{Law Lords}, but has no real opinion of her and finds her a little intimidating.

@UUID[Actor.0hUeYuOTIij6fMt4]{Isolde Begegnen} - High Matriarch: Rather fond of her, as she petitions him gently on behalf of the poor. While he doesn’t provide much support, he enjoys her attention.

Deadly Secret: A Powder Problem

About ten months ago, the Chancellor saw Law Lord @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} inhaling a white powder. Saying it was a simple tonic, Wasmeier offered some to Sparsam, who found its effects beneficial. Wasmeier introduced him to @UUID[JournalEntry.orDqA8A9sQXPHycl.JournalEntryPage.6uIwjhXBIJYEMFLo#secret-identities]{‘Frau Kenner’}, who has kept him supplied with it since then. Unknown to the Chancellor, the doses he received were spiced with some highly-addictive extras. When Sparsam became worried, Wasmeier waved his concerns away, saying that @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.jTFOrokjEHbi12rT]{Ranald’s Delight} was completely non-addictive unless abused. This astute reply played on Sparsam’s puritanical character, and the guilt-ridden Chancellor is now convinced that his own moral weakness created the problem.

Initially in favour of the tax changes, Sparsam changed his mind at the first demonstrations, but as soon as he voiced his concerns, Frau Kenner told him that her supply depended on his continued support of the taxes. If challenged, Sparsam will either leave or have the Characters thrown out, but he will be grateful for a friendly, sympathetic ear. If questioned gently, Sparsam will eventually break down: between sobs, he expresses guilt over his addiction, and the trouble he has caused by supporting the taxes. If the Characters have not offered to do so already, Sparsam will implore them to help him.

All Sparsam knows about Frau Kenner is that she visits him once a week, the next visit is due on the last day of the Carnival. He describes her as ‘about 30, 5 and a half feet tall, with long blonde hair.’ Sparsam will also inform the Characters that he gave her a pass to the Inner Palace.

Carnival Events

Day 1 Wellentag: @UUID[JournalEntry.qnddoqf7stZdPo0E.JournalEntryPage.ZECt3XSYZJJ0qmEe#operatic-recitals-(wellentag,-7–10:00-p.m.)]{Operatic Recitals}
